name: AddEventHandler
summary: Listens for a local event.
description: Registers a callback on the current resource's local event bus. The handler is owned by the current resource generation and is discarded automatically when that generation stops or reloads; it never receives network traffic unless the event was separately registered as a network event.

name: ClearTimeout
summary: Cancels a timer created by `SetTimeout`.
description: Cancels a pending timeout owned by the current resource generation. It returns `false` when the id is unknown or the callback has already begun; cancelling cannot interrupt a callback that is currently running.

name: CreateThread
summary: Starts a coroutine managed by the host.
description: Its body may call `Wait`, which an ordinary function cannot.
example:
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        print(Open77.character.speed())
        Wait(1000)
    end
end)

name: DeleteResourceKvp
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.kvp.delete`.
description: FiveM-familiar alias for `Open77.kvp.delete`. It atomically removes only the named key owned by the calling resource and reports whether that key existed.

name: GetCurrentResourceName
summary: Name of the current resource.
description: Returns the immutable manifest name of the resource whose Lua VM is executing. Use it for diagnostics and namespacing, not as a mutable display label.

name: GetInvokingResource
summary: Real caller of the currently executing export.
description: Returns nil outside an export callback. Use this value for service ownership instead of accepting a forgeable owner argument.

name: GetInvokingResourceGeneration
summary: Generation of the resource invoking the current export.
description: Returns nil outside an export callback. A changed generation lets a service retire handles left by an older VM.

name: GetResourceKvp
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.kvp.get`.
description: FiveM-familiar alias for `Open77.kvp.get`. It returns the original stored Lua type or nil when absent and stays inside the active connection-address and calling-resource namespace.

name: GetResourceState
summary: State of a resource.
description: Reads the lifecycle state currently known by the client resource host. This is a snapshot only: it does not start, stop, or wait for the target resource.

name: RegisterKeyMapping
summary: Declares a named, rebindable action bound to a key.
description: Declares a named, rebindable action bound to a key, as an engine primitive. Requires `input.actions`. Accepts a spec table `{ id, name, key, hold, onPressed, onReleased }` or the positional form `(id, name, key, onPressed [, onReleased])`; the callback receives the mapping id, fires on the key-down edge (and key-up in hold mode), and never fires while a page owns the keyboard. Returns the effective key (the player's saved rebind, else the default). The player rebinds it from Pause -> Settings -> KEY BINDINGS, and the choice persists machine-globally across servers and relaunches. Mirrored as `Open77.input.registerKeyMapping`.

name: RegisterNetEvent
summary: Allows an event to arrive from the server.
description: Allows an authenticated server event with this name to enter the current resource, and optionally attaches a handler in the same call. Registration is generation-scoped, requires `network.events`, and does not turn arbitrary client events into server events.

name: RemoveEventHandler
summary: Removes a handler.
description: Removes the exact callback previously registered for the named local event. It returns `false` when that event/callback pair is not owned by the current resource generation.

name: SetResourceKvp
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.kvp.set`.
description: FiveM-familiar alias for `Open77.kvp.set`. It stores one typed value in the calling resource's persistent namespace for the active connection address; it cannot select another server or resource.

name: SetTimeout
summary: Runs a function once, later.
description: Schedules a Lua callback after at least the requested number of milliseconds without blocking the game thread. The timer belongs to the current resource generation and is cancelled automatically on stop or hot reload.

name: TriggerEvent
summary: Fires a local event.
description: Dispatches an event only inside the client resource runtime. Arguments must fit the runtime's bounded script-value representation; use `TriggerServerEvent` for traffic that must cross the network.

name: TriggerServerEvent
summary: Sends an event to the server.
description: Serializes and sends an event to the connected server with the caller's authenticated player identity. It requires `network.events`; tables must be serializable and payload limits are enforced before anything is queued.

name: Wait
summary: Suspends the current coroutine.
description: Only usable inside a `CreateThread`.

name: exports
summary: Declares a function callable by other resources.
description: Publishes a named function from the current resource so another resource can call it through `Open77.exports.call`. The registration is tied to the current generation, so stale functions cannot survive a stop or hot reload.

name: print
summary: Writes to the Open77 log, prefixed with the resource name.
description: Writes a resource-prefixed line to the Open77 log. Values are converted with bounded formatting; this does not send a chat message or write into a WebUI page.

name: require
summary: Loads a local Lua module or a published dependency library into the caller's client VM.
description: Client-only Lua module loader. Loads a local module, or a published module from a declared, running dependency using `@provider` / `@provider/module`. The dependency form requires the development client update introduced with PolyZone. Dots map to folders; omit `.lua`. Code executes synchronously in the caller's VM, permissions and budget. Results are cached by resolved file per caller generation; no returned value becomes `true`. Lookup/loading failures return `nil, reason`; circular imports are rejected. Reload consumers to adopt changed library code. Unlike exports, no live Lua object crosses a VM boundary. No HTTP, native `package` loader or unrestricted filesystem access is exposed; the dedicated-server sandbox has no `require`.
returns: module value (true when no value is returned), or nil on loading failure
example:
local PZ, reason = require('@polyzone')
assert(PZ, reason)
local zone = PZ.CircleZone:Create({x=100, y=200, z=20}, 15, {name='meeting_point'})

name: await
summary: Waits for a promise to settle.
description: Only usable inside a `CreateThread`.

name: status
summary: State of the promise, without waiting.
description: Returns the promise state without yielding the current coroutine. Use it for polling or diagnostics; `await()` remains the normal way to receive a completed export result.

name: clear
summary: Removes every world anchor owned by the calling resource.
description: Other resources are unaffected. Anchors are also cleared automatically on stop, reload, world exit, and when their page is destroyed.

name: create
summary: Anchors a world point, projected by the plugin on every game frame.
description:
No permission of its own: the capability is the one `Open77.camera.project` already grants ungated, with the sampling moved off the Lua tick.

Options require exactly one of `position` (a fixed world point) or `entity` (followed live, with an optional world-axis `offset`) -- passing both, or neither, is refused with `position_or_entity_required`. They also accept `tag` (`[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, 32 bytes), `maxDistance` (default 100.0), `minDistance` (default 0.0) and `visible` (default true).

`render` selects the delivery and is fixed for the anchor's life: `page` (the default) publishes coordinates to a WebUI page, while `card`, `ring` and `dot` are drawn natively by the plugin in the frame that presents them. `page` is REQUIRED only for `render = "page"`; a native style has nowhere to publish and needs no surface at all, though a page passed alongside one is still ownership-checked. A page this resource does not own is refused with `stale_or_unowned_page`.

Native styles take a `presentation` table: `label`, `sublabel` (192 bytes each), `key` (`card` only, 8 bytes), `color`, `accent`, `background` (`#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`; anything else is refused as `invalid_color` / `invalid_accent` / `invalid_background`), `scale`, `thickness`, `radius` and `groundOffset` (`ring`), `progress` (`card`; negative draws no bar) and `showDistance`. The colour defaults are the OPEN//77 design tokens -- `color` `#F2F6F8`, `accent` `#22D8E2`, `background` `#0A1220F0` -- and they matter more than defaults usually do, because `presentation` is patched whole: see `Open77.anchors.update`.

The batched `open77:anchors` event a page receives is the COMPLETE set for that surface; an id that is absent is hidden, out of its distance band, behind the camera, or its entity is not streamed. Treat absence as gone rather than holding the last coordinate. Limits are 32 anchors per resource and 128 in total.

name: list
summary: Lists the calling resource's world anchors with their last projection.
description: Each snapshot carries its requested definition plus `render` (echoing its style), `resolved` (where the anchor actually was on the last frame -- for an entity anchor the live transform plus the offset, not what was registered) and `screen` (`x`, `y` normalised to [0..1] with a top-left origin, and `depth` in metres in front of the camera), `distance`, `onScreen`, and `projected`. An invisible anchor is still projected and still listed, so this stays the way to decide which of a resource's world points deserve one of its 32 slots.
returns: array of { id, tag, kind, render, entity, offset, surface, maxDistance, minDistance, visible, projected, onScreen, distance, position, resolved, screen }, or nil

name: remove
summary: Removes one resource-owned world anchor.
description: Removing an unknown handle succeeds, so teardown is idempotent.

name: update
summary: Patches a resource-owned world anchor.
description:
Top-level fields are patched individually: only what you supply changes. **`presentation` is the exception and is patched WHOLE.** `update(handle, { presentation = { label = "Locked" } })` does not keep the colours you set at creation -- it resets `color`, `accent`, `background` and every other presentation field to its default. Always resend the complete presentation table, or keep it in a local and patch that. A prompt changes its label, its key and its hold progress on the same frame or not at all, which is why the table has one dirty flag rather than eleven.

Neither `page` nor the anchor's kind is patchable; patching a field the kind does not own -- `position` on an entity anchor, `entity` or `offset` on a position anchor -- is refused with `anchor_kind_mismatch` rather than ignored. `render` is fixed at creation and a patch carrying it is refused with `render_is_not_patchable`. Re-pointing an entity anchor at a new `entity` is supported, which is the respawn case. Ownership prevents mutation of another resource's anchor.

name: cancel
summary: Cancel the local player's RP action and pending requests.
description: Stops local presentation and queues a reliable self-cancellation request. Omitting playbackId also abandons pending starts; late acceptances are cancelled. Supply the ID from request() or sequence() in delayed callbacks so they cannot stop a replacement action. A mismatched active ID rejects with stale_playback. Resolving true means cancellation was queued (or nothing was active), not that the server has acknowledged the stop; observe onPlayerAnimationChanged for authoritative state. A player may cancel their own server-started action, never another player's action. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to true when cancellation is queued or already inactive
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.cancel()
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local cancelled, rejected = pending:await()
    if not cancelled then print(rejected) end
end)

name: current
summary: The clip a body is currently playing.
description: Returns false when it is playing nothing — which is a state, not an error.

name: get
summary: Look up one RP profile without starting playback.
description: Resolves to a copy of the profile, including its default clip and exact allowed variants. Profile IDs are case-sensitive. An unknown ID resolves to nil without an error; check the second await result to distinguish a failed request from a missing profile. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to a profile table, or nil when absent
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.get('smoke')
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local profile, rejected = pending:await()
    if rejected then print(rejected); return end
    if profile then print(profile.clip, #profile.clips) end
end)

name: list
summary: Find synchronized RP animation profiles in the local catalogue.
description: Resolves to copied profile definitions containing id, label, category, default clip and allowed clips. The optional query is a case-insensitive substring across ID, label and category, up to 128 characters. An empty query returns all 15 profiles; no match returns an empty array. Catalogue membership and male/female rig bindings are not proof of native playback validation. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to a profile array
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.list('social')
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local profiles, rejected = pending:await()
    if not profiles then print(rejected); return end
    for _, profile in ipairs(profiles) do print(profile.id, profile.label) end
end)

name: play
summary: Plays a named animation on a body.
description: Does not work on the local player: their body cannot hold a workspot. Use `Open77.animations.playSelf` for that, which stands a double in for them.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.animations.play(entityId, "emote_smoke")
if not ok then print("refused: " .. reason) end

name: playSelf
summary: Plays an emote on the local player, through a stand-in body.
description: The player's own body cannot hold a workspot, so an invisible double takes their place for the length of the clip. This is a separate call rather than `play` with the player's id because the mechanism is genuinely different.

name: request
summary: Request a synchronized RP action for the local player.
description: The server validates the named profile and returns a playback state and playbackId; acceptance does not mean the native workspot has mounted. Options are clip, durationMs and loop only. The clip must belong to the profile. loop defaults to true; omitted or zero duration is indefinite when looping. With loop=false the default is 5000 ms. A nonzero duration must be an integer from 1000 to 600000 ms. Playback temporarily uses the F7 third-person body without changing the saved camera preference. Moving, combat and unsafe player states interrupt it. Use cancel(), not the legacy local stop(entity), for synchronized actions. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to the server-accepted playback state
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected or timed out
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.request('smoke', { loop = false, durationMs = 15000 })
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local playback, rejected = pending:await()
    if not playback then print(rejected); return end
    print('Accepted action: ' .. playback.playbackId)
end)

name: sequence
summary: Request an ordered RP sequence for the local player.
description: Accepts 1–16 steps with profile, optional clip and durationMs. Each step defaults to 5000 ms, must last 1000–600000 ms, and the total cannot exceed 600000 ms. The only sequence option is loop, default false. These are server scheduling durations, not measured clip lengths. Profile changes use asynchronous workspot exit/re-entry, not guaranteed seamless blends. The result is authoritative acceptance, not a native rendering acknowledgement. Unlike the server method, this call takes no playerId. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to the server-accepted playback state
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected

name: state
summary: Read the last active RP state visible to this client.
description: Defaults to the local player, or accepts a visible player's network ID. Resolves to a copied canonical state, or nil when inactive or unavailable. It does not query arbitrary players outside the routing bucket or verify native rendering. Fields include playerId, playbackId, epoch, revision, active, steps, loop and step timing. On the client, onPlayerAnimationChanged receives this state as a Lua table; the server event instead passes JSON. Do not use a client observation to grant authoritative rewards. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to active playback state, or nil when unavailable
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.state()
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local state, rejected = pending:await()
    if rejected then print(rejected); return end
    if state then print(state.playbackId, state.active) end
end)

name: stop
summary: Stops whatever a body is playing and releases what was set up for it.
description: Stops the workspot animation currently managed by Open77 for the selected body and releases its native animation state. It does not claim or stop arbitrary game animations that Open77 does not own.

name: stopSelf
summary: Stops the local player's emote and removes the stand-in.
description: Ends the local-player emote created by `playSelf` and removes its stand-in body. Cleanup is idempotent and is also performed when the owning resource generation stops.

name: apply
summary: Applies a previously captured appearance snapshot to the local player.
description: Requires `player.appearance.edit`. The runtime validates the schema, build, catalog digest, gender, option identities, choice bounds, and duplicates before touching the game.

name: capture
summary: Captures the local player's complete validated appearance snapshot.
description: Requires `player.appearance.read`. The snapshot is bound to schema version 1, game build 2.31, a catalog digest, gender hash, and at most 256 head/body/arms options.
returns: table { schemaVersion, gameBuild, catalogDigest, gender, options }, or nil

name: captureBody
summary: Capture the local native body appearance groups.
description: Requires player.appearance.read. Returns {family,groups}, with native part/name hashes and resource key pairs. This readback is for trusted projection services, not a committed character edit or visual proof. Use the selected durable identity adapter for persistence.
example:
local body, err = Open77.appearance.captureBody()
if body then print(body.family, #body.groups) else print(err) end

name: finishCommit
summary: Finishes the current appearance commit transaction.
description: Requires `player.appearance.edit`. Call after a successful apply/persistence flow so the native editor can release its commit state.

name: isOpen
summary: Whether the local appearance editor is open.
description: Requires `player.appearance.read`; returns false when the permission or backend is unavailable.

name: open
summary: Opens the local Cyberpunk appearance editor.
description: Requires `player.appearance.edit`. The optional value may be a mode string or `{ mode = string }`; `ripperdoc` is used by default.

name: switchBodyFamily
summary: Starts a guarded body-family transition.
description: Starts a guarded transition to the requested body family and optionally resumes the native editor afterward. It requires player.appearance.edit; completion is consumed with takeBodyFamilyTransition.

name: takeBodyFamilyTransition
summary: Consumes the pending body-family transition result.
description: Consumes the pending body-family transition result once, returning its serialized payload or nil while no result is ready. It requires player.appearance.edit.

name: list
summary: Lists generic files declared by the current resource.
description: Returns the resource files declared by the current manifest. It is an allow-list view, not a directory listing, and does not grant access to undeclared files or arbitrary paths.

name: texture
summary: Validates a declared PNG texture for resource APIs.
description: The path must match the manifest's `files` allowlist. PNG textures are limited to 512 KiB and 512 by 512 pixels.
returns: descriptor { type, asset, mime, width, height, bytes }, or nil

name: attachToEntity
summary: Makes a blip follow an Open77 entity.
description: Changes an owned blip from a fixed world position to tracking a streamed Open77 entity. The entity id is ephemeral and the call requires `ui.vanilla.map`; remove or reattach the blip when its gameplay target changes.

name: clear
summary: Removes every blip owned by the current resource.
description: Removes every vanilla-map blip owned by the calling resource generation. Other resources' blips are left untouched, and generation teardown performs the same cleanup automatically.

name: create
summary: Creates a resource-owned vanilla map pin.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.map`. Provide exactly one of `position` or `entity`. Set `routable = true` on a positional blip to use Cyberpunk's trusted custom-waypoint definition; its sprite becomes `CustomPositionVariant` and `track(id)` can then start native GPS routing. The returned 64-bit generation handle is a decimal string and is cleaned up automatically when the resource stops.

params.name: options
params.type: table { position|entity, sprite?, label?, icon?, active?, visibleThroughWalls?, routable?, slot?, offset? }

name: get
summary: Reads one blip owned by the current resource.
description: Returns a read-only snapshot of one blip owned by the calling resource. The handle must still belong to the current generation; a stale or foreign id is rejected.

name: list
summary: Lists blips owned by the current resource.
description: Lists snapshots of all vanilla-map blips owned by the calling resource generation. The returned tables are copies and changing them does not mutate the map.

name: remove
summary: Removes one owned blip.
description: Deletes one blip owned by the calling resource and invalidates its handle. Removal is resource-scoped, so one package cannot erase another package's map state.

name: setActive
summary: Activates or deactivates a vanilla mappin.
description: Updates the active/highlighted state of an owned vanilla-map blip. This changes presentation only and does not create a route or change server state.

name: setDescription
summary: Sets the custom fullscreen-map description of an owned blip.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.map`. The description is displayed by Open77's fullscreen-map tooltip for the selected native mappin.

name: setIcon
summary: Sets a declared PNG icon or restores the native sprite.
description: Accepts a path, a texture descriptor, `{ asset, size }`, or false. The native mappin remains underneath for map selection, routing, tooltips, and fallback.

name: setLabel
summary: Changes the fullscreen-map tooltip title.
description: Open77 keeps the label in private script data, independent from the vanilla variant's generic title.

name: setPosition
summary: Moves a blip to a world position.
description: Also detaches an entity-following blip.

name: setSprite
summary: Changes the vanilla mappin variant.
description: Accepts an exact 2.31 variant name, a stable alias, or an integer from 0 through 146. See `wiki/blips.md` for the complete list.

name: setTitle
summary: Sets the custom fullscreen-map title of an owned blip.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.map`. This is the semantic title alias of `setLabel`; the HUD does not permanently render it beside the icon.

name: setTrackingAlternative
summary: Sets another owned blip as the routing alternative.
description: Passing nil clears it. This does not force the world-map controller to start tracking.

name: setVisibleThroughWalls
summary: Changes vanilla through-wall visibility.
description: Controls whether an owned world marker remains visible when geometry occludes it. The setting affects presentation on this client only and requires `ui.vanilla.map`.

name: sprites
summary: Lists every usable mappin variant in the current build.
description: Returns 147 entries for Cyberpunk 2077 2.31. This metadata query does not require map mutation permission.

name: track
summary: Selects this blip as the vanilla manually tracked destination.
description: Follows the same internal `MappinSystem` operation as selecting a pin on the fullscreen map. This changes the tracked id; native road calculation additionally requires the blip to have been created with `routable = true`. Returns `changed = false` when this blip is already tracked.

name: untrack
summary: Safely clears manual tracking for this blip.
description: The native action is invoked only if this owned blip is currently tracked, so a resource cannot untrack a quest or another system's pin.

name: update
summary: Updates several properties of an owned blip.
description: A replacement mappin is registered before the previous one is removed. `position` switches to positional mode; `entity` switches to attached mode.

name: aimRay
summary: The ray from the camera along its forward vector: what the reticle points at.
description: `Open77.camera.view()` plus `Open77.world.raycast` in one call. Unlike `Open77.inspector.target`, which answers with an entity under the crosshair or nothing, this hits empty pavement too, which is what placing a prop, a blip or a teleport target needs. `maxDistance` defaults to 200 m and is capped at 5000. Requires `world.query`.
returns: table { hit, position, normal, material, distance }, or nil
reason: permission_denied:world.query, invalid_distance, camera_unavailable, or the engine status
example:
local ray = Open77.camera.aimRay(100)
if ray and ray.hit then Open77.blips.create({ position = ray.position, label = "Here" }) end

name: attach
summary: Reattaches the camera to the body.
description: Attaches the Open77 camera to a game entity using the supplied local offset and rotation. Camera ownership is local to the resource generation; attaching replaces the resource's previous detached/attached camera state.

name: clearOrbit
summary: Releases this resource's preview orbit and framing.
description: Client-only; requires camera.preview. Refuses another resource's preview. Succeeds harmlessly when no resource preview is owned. Resource stop also clears its preview.

name: detach
summary: Detaches the camera from the body, with an offset in the body's own space.
description: Detaches the Open77 camera from its target while retaining a controllable camera view. It does not synchronize a camera to other players and is automatically restored during resource cleanup.

name: orbit
summary: Sets this resource's preview orbit yaw on an active third-person rig.
description: Client-only; requires camera.preview. yawDegrees must be finite and is normalized modulo 360. Requires an engaged, unsuspended Open77 third-person camera; it does not switch perspectives. One resource owns the preview, and another owner is refused. Repeated calls update the same preview. clearOrbit or resource stop releases it.

name: project
summary: Projects a world point into normalized WebUI viewport coordinates.
description: Uses REDengine's active camera projection. `(0,0)` is the top-left and `(1,1)` the bottom-right. `onScreen` is false for points behind the view or beyond the viewport.
returns: table { x, y, depth, distance, onScreen }, or nil

name: setFov
summary: Sets the field of view, in degrees.
description: Changes the field of view of the camera currently controlled by Open77. The value is validated by the native backend and applies only to this client's presentation.
example: Open77.camera.setFov(90)

name: thirdPerson
summary: Controls the legacy camera-only third-person path.
description: Legacy camera-only control, not the playable perspective arbiter. Prefer `Open77.perspective.setThirdPerson(enabled, force)` to switch or lock the playable FPP/TPP view, and `Open77.camera.configureThirdPerson(options)` for shoulder framing, anchors, movement FOV and shake. The legacy call changes the camera without coordinating all body, weapon and input owners. Turning it off restores the view the game had before the call, rather than some default.
example:
-- A shoulder view during the fashion show, restored afterwards
AddEventHandler("show:started", function() Open77.camera.thirdPerson(true, 2.5, 1.7) end)
AddEventHandler("show:ended", function() Open77.camera.thirdPerson(false) end)

name: view
summary: Where the view is: position, forward vector, field of view.
description: Returns the latest game-thread camera snapshot used by projection and presentation APIs. It is a same-client read and may return `nil, reason` while the game camera is unavailable.

name: animation
summary: The animation currently playing on this character.
description: Reads the current animation snapshot for an entity, or for the local player when omitted. The result is observational and can change on the next frame; it does not grant animation ownership.

name: groundSpeed
summary: Speed projected on the ground, without the vertical component.
description: Returns horizontal movement speed for the selected character, excluding vertical velocity. Entity ids refer to the current client stream and must not be persisted as server identity.

name: health
summary: Current health.
description: Reads the engine-side health visible for the selected character on this client. For replicated player gameplay rules use the server-authoritative player health APIs; this helper is a presentation snapshot, not authority.

name: isAlive
summary: Whether the character is alive.
description: Reports the current engine alive/dead flag for the selected character. It is useful for presentation and diagnostics but may lag the authoritative server health transition by a replication frame.

name: isArmed
summary: Whether a weapon is drawn.
description: Reports whether the selected character is currently considered armed by the game presentation state. It does not enumerate inventory or prove that a weapon action is server-authorized.

name: isCrouched
summary: Whether the character is crouching.
description: Reads the character's current crouch presentation flag. Omit the entity to inspect the local player; remote values exist only while that proxy is streamed.

name: isDriver
summary: Whether they occupy the driver's seat.
description: Returns whether the selected character occupies the canonical driver seat of a vehicle. Use `seat()` when the exact seat and vehicle entity are also needed.

name: isEmoting
summary: Whether they hold a workspot (an emote is running).
description: Reports whether Open77 currently presents the character in an emote/workspot state. This is a transient local snapshot and is cleared with the owning presentation lifecycle.

name: isGrounded
summary: Whether the character is touching the ground.
description: Reads the engine grounded flag for the selected character. The value is sampled from the current client frame and should not be used alone for authoritative movement validation.

name: isInVehicle
summary: Whether the character is mounted in a vehicle.
description: Reports whether the character is mounted in a vehicle according to the current client presentation. Call `seat()` to retrieve the mounted slot and vehicle entity id.

name: isSliding
summary: Whether the character is sliding.
description: Reads the current sliding locomotion flag for the selected character. It is an observational state and does not start or stop a slide.

name: isVaulting
summary: Whether the character is vaulting.
description: Reads the current vaulting locomotion flag for the selected character. Remote values are available only while the corresponding proxy is streamed.

name: position
summary: The character's position.
description: Returns the character's current world-space coordinates from the game-thread snapshot. Omit the entity for the local player; do not persist a client entity id as a network identity.

name: seat
summary: The seat occupied in a vehicle, if any.
description: Returns the canonical seat name and the mounted vehicle's client entity id when the character is in a vehicle. A character that is not mounted returns `nil`; both values are snapshots and the entity id is valid only in the current client stream.
returns: seat name and vehicle entity id, or nil
reason when the character could not be read

name: speed
summary: Instantaneous speed, all components.
description: Returns total character movement speed, including vertical motion, from the latest local snapshot. Use `groundSpeed()` when only horizontal locomotion is relevant.

name: state
summary: One complete snapshot of a character.
description:
A single engine pass fills the whole record even when the caller only wanted the speed. That is deliberate: every field then describes the **same instant**, so a caller cannot see a body grounded and airborne in the same breath.

With no argument, answers about the local player.
returns: table { isPlayer, attached, id, engineId, position, orientation, forward, velocity, speed, groundSpeed, yaw, alive, health, grounded, crouched, sliding, vaulting, air, fall, landing, weapon…, inVehicle, seat, driver }
reason, when the first is nil
example:
local s = Open77.character.state()
if s.inVehicle and s.driver then
    print("driving at " .. math.floor(s.speed) .. " u/s")
end

name: weapon
summary: The equipped weapon and its state.
description: Returns the drawn weapon's recognized item id and category for the selected character. It returns `nil` when no recognized weapon is currently presented and does not expose or mutate inventory.
returns: reason when the character could not be read

name: yaw
summary: Horizontal orientation, in degrees.
description: Returns the selected character's current world yaw in degrees. The value is a presentation snapshot and should be normalized by the caller when computing angular deltas.

name: setText
summary: Writes UTF-8 text to the operating-system clipboard.
description: Client-only and requires `clipboard.write` on the resource whose VM performs the call. Text is limited to 256 KiB, must be valid UTF-8 and cannot contain an embedded NUL. The operation is write-only: resources cannot inspect the user's existing clipboard. A temporarily owned clipboard returns `false, clipboard_busy`; callers should let the player retry instead of polling every frame.
example: local ok, reason = Open77.clipboard.setText("position = { x = 1, y = 2, z = 3 }")

name: attackState
summary: Read local native Gorilla melee activity.
description: Requires player.cyberware.read. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Returns {sequence,holding,variant,record,chargeExpired} when a usable native Gorilla weapon is observed; unavailable/unarmed states return nil, reason. This is client observation, not authoritative charge, damage or cooldown. The platform forwards bounded intent and the server validates it.
example:
local state = Open77.cyberware.attackState()
if state then print(state.sequence, state.holding, state.chargeExpired) end

name: captureArms
summary: Capture the local native Gorilla Arms posture profiles.
description: Requires player.cyberware.read. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Returns {family,groups}; groups contain part/name hashes and key pairs. The validated adapter supplies matching holstered and drawn alternatives for male or female, not arbitrary replacement assets. Native readiness and equipment readback do not prove rendered geometry.
example:
local profile, err = Open77.cyberware.captureArms()
if not profile then print(err); return end
print(profile.family, #profile.groups)

name: configureLocal
summary: Configure native charge limits and stamina-override presence.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Requires the same owned ready request. options accepts nullable normalStaminaCost/chargedStaminaCost (0..300) and maxChargeMs (100..60000, default10000). Native code uses cost presence to suppress supported native attack prices; the server owns the actual costs and debits. It does not grant stamina or suppress unrelated movement costs.

name: localState
summary: Read the native equipment projection state for an owned request.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Returns a phase string and a reason string: pending, ready or failed for the matching native request. Invalid/foreign native requests may return an empty phase plus reason; Lua permission/argument failures return nil, reason. ready describes native equipment readback, not SQL commit or visible confirmation.
returns: nil, reason on Lua validation failure
example:
local phase, reason = Open77.cyberware.localState(request)
if phase == "failed" or not phase or phase == "" then print(reason) end

name: presentArms
summary: Project or clear an owned Gorilla Arms appearance overlay.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. playerId is the network player ID, including the local player for its self-view. Pass a validated captured {family,groups} profile, or false to clear. Overlay ownership survives identical replays; conflicting owners fail. Native attachment/posture work is asynchronous; true is acceptance, not visible completion.
example:
local profile, err = Open77.cyberware.captureArms()
if profile then
    local ok, reason = Open77.cyberware.presentArms(playerId, profile)
    if not ok then print(reason) end
end

name: projectLocal
summary: Queue native local Gorilla equipment installation or removal.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. enabled=true equips the supported native arms; false restores bare arms. Returns an owned positive integer request ID. Poll localState(request); queued work is neither a committed purchase nor visual proof. Resource stop releases the native owner.
example:
local request, err = Open77.cyberware.projectLocal(true)
if not request then print(err); return end
-- The platform projector correlates native readiness with the server ticket.
print(Open77.cyberware.localState(request))

name: command
summary: Runs one registered native laboratory command directly.
description: Requires `debug.runtime` and the trusted `open77_debug` owner. Input is limited to 4096 bytes and unknown commands are not forwarded to the server.
returns: true and command result on success

name: eval
summary: Compiles and executes a bounded text-only Lua chunk in the privileged debug VM.
description: Requires `debug.runtime` and the trusted `open77_debug` owner. Source is limited to 32 KiB, the optional chunk label to 64 bytes, returned values to 16 and result text to 8 KiB. The ordinary memory, instruction and frame-time quotas remain active.
returns: true and bounded result text on success

name: redscript
summary: Queues one bounded command through the REDscript debug bridge.
description: Requires `debug.runtime` and the trusted `open77_debug` owner. The opaque command is limited to 4096 bytes and executes from a genuine REDscript frame.
returns: true and bridge result on success

name: aimed
summary: The streamed door currently under the crosshair.
description: Requires `world.doors`. The returned `id` is an opaque 64-bit REDengine identity encoded as a string; never convert it to a Lua number. A successful discovery also makes that door addressable by `state` and the command functions while it remains streamed.
returns: reason when the first is nil
example:
local door, reason = Open77.doors.aimed()
if door then
    print(door.id, door.open, door.locked, door.distance)
end

name: aimedAny
summary: Reads the entity currently under the crosshair even when it is not a controllable Door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Unlike `aimed`, this controller-agnostic probe accepts static and scenery door meshes. It always provides identity and placement when targeting succeeds; open, locked, and sealed state is populated only when the entity exposes a door controller.

name: available
summary: Whether the client door backend is available.
description: This capability check does not discover or stream a door. Door operations require the `world.doors` permission.

name: clearInteractionPolicy
summary: Removes this resource's interaction policy for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Other resources' policies are unaffected.

name: close
summary: Closes a door.
description: Alias of `setOpen(door, false, force)`. Requires `world.doors`; application is asynchronous.

name: closest
summary: The closest streamed door around the local player.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Uses the same 0.5 to 100 metre player-centered query as `near`.
returns: reason when the first is nil

name: grantKey
summary: Grants an entity an opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Uses the door controller's native token mechanism rather than a parallel Open77 key list. This grants authorization but does not lock or deny an otherwise usable door; access enforcement belongs to `setInteractionAllowed`.

name: hasKey
summary: Whether an entity holds an opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`.
returns: reason when the first is nil

name: holders
summary: The entities holding an opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Holder IDs are opaque strings for the same precision reason as door IDs. Tokens are vanilla authorization data, not a global lock rule: an unlocked interactive door remains usable with no token. Combine `hasKey` with `setInteractionAllowed` when implementing an ox_doorlock-style policy.
returns: array of opaque entity ids, or nil
reason when the first is nil

name: lock
summary: Locks a door.
description: Alias of `setLocked(door, true, force)`.

name: near
summary: All streamed doors around the local player.
description: Requires `world.doors`. The radius is centered on the player and must be between 0.5 and 100 metres. Results are sorted nearest first and register each door for later ID-based operations.
returns: array of door snapshots, or nil
reason when the first is nil

name: open
summary: Opens a door.
description: Alias of `setOpen(door, true, force)`. Requires `world.doors`; application is asynchronous.

name: reset
summary: Resets a door to its configured default state.
description: Requires `world.doors`; queues the vanilla `ResetDoorState` event.

name: revokeKey
summary: Revokes an entity's opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`.

name: seal
summary: Seals a door.
description: Alias of `setSealed(door, true, force)`.

name: setAutomaticClose
summary: Enables or disables a door's automatic closing behavior.
description: Requires `world.doors`; queues the vanilla `SetCloseItself` event.

name: setInteractionAllowed
summary: Pre-declares whether vanilla interaction may open a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. The decision is synchronous when the game interacts with the door. Policies are owned by the resource, all active policies must allow, and they are removed automatically on stop/reload. `open77:doorInteract` is an observational event with `(doorId, activatorId, "true"|"false")`; it is too late to change that interaction.
example:
Open77.doors.setInteractionAllowed(doorId, playerHasAccess)
AddEventHandler("open77:doorInteract", function(door, activator, allowed)
    print(door, activator, allowed)
end)

name: setLocked
summary: Sets whether a door is locked.
description: Requires `world.doors`. `force` uses the vanilla quest-authority action; application is asynchronous.

name: setOpen
summary: Sets whether a door is open.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Success means the REDscript action was accepted; application is asynchronous and may take up to 200 ms. `force` uses the vanilla quest-authority action.

name: setSealed
summary: Sets whether a door is sealed.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Sealing is distinct from locking. `force` uses the vanilla quest-authority action.

name: setState
summary: Sets a door state by name.
description: Accepted states: `open`, `closed`, `locked`, `unlocked`, `sealed`, `unsealed`. Requires `world.doors`; `force` selects the quest-authority action.

name: sink
summary: Moves a static or scenery door below the floor.
description: Requires `world.doors`. This is a visual removal fallback for geometry that has no DoorControllerPS and therefore cannot be opened normally. Depth must be greater than zero and no more than 100 metres; the default is 3 metres.

name: state
summary: A live snapshot of a streamed door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Reads the live `DoorControllerPS`, never a fabricated default from the save record. Returns `door_not_streamed` after the entity unloads. Snapshot fields include `id`, `class`, `name`, `position`, `distance`, `open`, `closed`, `locked`, `sealed`, `busy`, `playerAuthorised`, `automaticClose`, toggle capabilities, shutter/lift flags, type/sides and opening speed/time.
returns: reason when the first is nil

name: unlock
summary: Unlocks a door.
description: Alias of `setLocked(door, false, force)`.

name: unseal
summary: Unseals a door.
description: Alias of `setSealed(door, false, force)`.

name: all
summary: Lists every replicated elevator state visible to the client.
description: Requires `elevators.read`; returns an empty array when the capability or backend is unavailable.

name: get
summary: Reads one replicated elevator by Open77 ID.
description: Requires `elevators.read`. Elevator IDs are server-assigned and should be kept unchanged.
returns: table { id, revision, bucket, engineEntity, activeFloor, originFloor, targetFloor, floorCount, travelMs, remainingMs, flags, phase, position, streamed, applied }, or nil

name: nearby
summary: Discovers streamed native elevators around the local player.
description: Requires `elevators.read`. Radius must be between 1 and 300 metres. Results distinguish unmanaged engine lifts from elevators already adopted by Open77.
returns: array of { engineEntity, controllerEntity, position, distance, managed, floorCount, activeFloor, id }

name: request
summary: Submits a floor request to the authoritative server.
description: Requires `elevators.request`. `action` is normally `call` or `goto`; the server validates the ID, floor, player bucket, range, state and policy.

name: getTime
summary: Lit l'horloge REDengine locale.
description: Primitive interne protégée par `world.environment`. Retourne un snapshot atomique de l'heure appliquée et de l'état de pause. Dans une session normale, utilisez l'export `open77_weather.getState` plutôt que cette valeur de projection.
returns: table { day, hour, minute, second, totalSeconds, frozen }, ou nil

name: isWeatherFrozen
summary: Indique si la météo automatique vanilla est neutralisée.
description: Demande `world.environment`.

name: setTime
summary: Projette une heure serveur dans REDengine.
description: Demande `world.environment`. `open77_weather` est normalement le seul propriétaire de cette permission. REDengine choisit la prochaine occurrence de l'heure demandée ; le package officiel filtre donc les petits reculs réseau pour éviter un saut d'un jour.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false

name: setTimeFrozen
summary: Fige ou libère uniquement l'horloge du jeu.
description: Ne fige pas la simulation. Demande `world.environment`; utilisé par la projection serveur pour neutraliser la vitesse vanilla.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false

name: setWeather
summary: Applique un preset météo REDengine.
description: Primitive interne demandant `world.environment`. Le second retour `applied=false` est aussi possible en cas de succès si le preset était déjà actif.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false
applied si succès, sinon raison du refus

name: setWeatherFrozen
summary: Désactive ou réactive le contrôleur météo automatique vanilla.
description: Demande `world.environment`. Figer conserve le preset courant et laisse le serveur décider du prochain événement.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false

name: apply
summary: Applies a table of local equipment slot values.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Values are record strings or false to clear. Options: allowRestricted=false and replace=false. With replace=false omitted slots are preserved; replace=true also clears omitted slots. Worn-set mutations run sequentially and may partially apply before an error; this is not an atomic transaction.

name: attached
summary: Reads the item actually attached at a local slot.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns a record string or false when no item is attached. Attachment alone does not prove the expected garment appearance has settled.
returns: record or false, or nil, reason

name: equip
summary: Equips a record in the local worn set.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Call equip(record[, slot][, options]); omitted slot is inferred by the native record adapter. options.allowRestricted defaults false. Read registry/attached/visualSettled separately when completion matters.

name: family
summary: Reads the local equipment body family.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns the native adapter body-family name, used to filter compatible records.

name: info
summary: Looks up metadata for one equipment record.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. The record name is 1..160 bytes. Result fields: record, tweakDbId, slot, attachmentSlot, catalogScope, supportsMale, supportsFemale, defaultSelectable and nonvisual. This lookup does not equip the item.

name: records
summary: Lists equipment records with optional slot and body-family filters.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Options: slot, family="male" or "female", restricted=false and limit=200 (positive integer, capped at 2000). restricted=true includes records not default-selectable; it does not grant mutation permission. Results use the same metadata shape as info().

name: registry
summary: Reads the local worn equipment slot registry.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns a table keyed by slot: record strings or false for empty slots. Registry state is separate from the attached item and its settled visual appearance.

name: slots
summary: Lists the supported clothing slot names and attachment slots.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns nine {name, attachmentSlot} entries: Head, Face, InnerChest, OuterChest, Legs, Feet, Outfit, UnderwearTop and UnderwearBottom.

name: tags
summary: Reads native tags associated with a local equipment slot.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns an array of tag strings for the current wearer and slot.

name: unequip
summary: Removes equipment from a local worn slot.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Does not delete the inventory item. Read native visual readiness separately.

name: visualSettled
summary: Checks native visual readiness for an expected clothing slot value.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. expected must be a record string or false. Reads registry/outfit visibility and actual attachment/appearance readiness; false means not yet settled, whereas nil, reason indicates an error. This native readback is not screenshot proof.

name: emit
summary: Fires a local event.
description: Emits an event on the resource-local client bus and invokes matching local handlers. It never sends a packet; use the network event API for server communication.

name: off
summary: Removes a handler registered with `on`.
description: Unregisters a local event handler id previously returned by `on`/`AddEventHandler`. The id is the only argument -- there is no event name parameter. Handler ids are owned by a resource generation and cannot remove another resource's callback.

name: on
summary: Listens for a local event.
description: Same as the `AddEventHandler` global. Events emitted by the plugin — `open77:pauseKey`, `open77:inspector:on` — arrive here.

name: call
summary: Calls a function exported by another resource.
description: Schedules another running client resource's exported function and returns a generation-bound Promise. Arguments and results must be serializable; unavailable resources, missing exports, stale generations and scheduler saturation are returned immediately as `nil, reason`.

name: components
summary: Lists the supported stock HUD component names.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Returns canonical names suitable for `setVisible`, `isVisible`, or a complete custom-HUD replacement loop.
returns: array of canonical component names, or nil

name: isVisible
summary: Reads the effective visibility of one stock HUD component.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. The result already combines hide claims from every resource. Aliases such as `map`, `time`, `hp`, `ammo`, `weaponAmmo`, and `speed` are accepted.

name: setVisible
summary: Hides or restores one stock HUD component for this resource.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Passing `false` adds this resource's hide claim; passing `true` releases only its own claim. Another resource may still keep the component hidden. Claims are released automatically when the resource stops or reloads. Canonical components are `minimap`, `compass`, `clock`, `health`, `stamina`, `weapon`, and `speedometer`.
example:
local ok, effective = Open77.hud.setVisible("minimap", false)
assert(ok, effective)

name: state
summary: Returns the complete effective stock-HUD visibility snapshot.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Keys always use canonical component names and values are booleans after all resources' claims have been combined.
returns: table keyed by canonical component name, or nil

name: isCaptured
summary: Whether another WebUI currently owns keyboard input.
description: Contextual actions should become inert while this is true so chat and menu typing cannot activate gameplay.

name: isDown
summary: Whether an allowlisted contextual action key is currently held.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Supported keys are A-Z, 0-9, F1-F12, SPACE, ENTER/RETURN, TAB, SHIFT, CTRL/CONTROL, ALT, CAPSLOCK, BACKSPACE, INSERT, DELETE, HOME, END, PAGEUP/PAGEDOWN, and arrows. Prefer a press edge or hold timer over firing every frame.
returns: reason when the key or permission is refused

name: keyFor
summary: The effective key of one of this resource's own mappings.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Returns the effective key (the player's rebind if any, otherwise the registered default) for a mapping id owned by the calling resource, or nil when no such mapping exists.
returns: key string, or nil when the id is not registered by this resource

name: mappings
summary: Every registered key mapping across all running resources.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Returns an array of `{ resource, id, name, key, defaultKey, hold, rebound }` records for the rebinding UI. Only serialisable metadata is exposed; the callbacks stay in their owning resource.

name: rebind
summary: Sets and persists a new key for any mapping.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Rebinds the mapping identified by `resource` and `id` to `key` (same key vocabulary as `Open77.input.isDown`), persists it machine-globally, and raises `open77:keybinds:changed`. Used by the pause KEY BINDINGS tab.

name: registerKeyMapping
summary: Declares a named, rebindable action bound to a key (twin of the RegisterKeyMapping global).
description: Requires `input.actions`. Accepts a spec table `{ id, name, key (or defaultKey), hold, onPressed, onReleased }` or the positional form `(id, name, key, onPressed [, onReleased])`. The engine owns the registry and the per-frame dispatch; the callback receives the mapping id and never fires while a page owns the keyboard. `onPressed` fires on the key-down edge; with `hold` (or a positional release callback) `onReleased` fires on key-up. Re-registering an id replaces the entry but keeps the player's saved rebind. Ids are letters/numbers/`_.:-`, up to 64 chars; names up to 96. Up to 64 mappings per resource.
returns: effective key (the saved rebind, else the default)

name: reset
summary: Restores a mapping to its registered default key.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Drops any saved override for the mapping identified by `resource` and `id`, restores the default key, persists the change, and raises `open77:keybinds:changed`.

name: setNativeActionBlocked
summary: Adds or removes this resource's block on the native map action.
description: Client-only; requires input.actions. Exactly two arguments are required, a string action and boolean blocked. Only "OpenMapMenu" is supported. Blocking is resource-owned: false removes only this resource's block, so another resource may keep the action blocked. Resource stop releases its block. This does not synthesize input or expose arbitrary native action suppression.

name: unregisterKeyMapping
summary: Removes a key mapping this resource declared.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Frees the mapping's callbacks and raises `open77:keybinds:changed`. Only affects mappings owned by the calling resource.
returns: boolean: true when a mapping was removed

name: enable
summary: Turns the permanent aim ray on or off.
description: Turning it off also clears the outline: the outline belongs to the session that asked for it and must not outlive it.
returns: reason, when the first is nil

name: outline
summary: Outlines the aimed object, independently of the ray.
description: Lets a caller read the target without painting the world. The outline uses `entRenderHighlightEvent`, the same event focus mode and scanning already use.
returns: reason, when the first is nil

name: target
summary: What the aim ray is currently pointing at.
description:
Reads a snapshot, never a probe. The ray has to be cast on the game thread, and the plugin refreshes it at 10 Hz, so calling this costs nothing and cannot land a raycast on the wrong thread.

Always returns a table when a game is present. `valid` separates "nothing in view" from "no game" — the latter returns `nil, reason`.
returns: table { valid, engineId, class, name, kind, position, distance }
reason, when the first is nil
example:
local t = Open77.inspector.target()
if t and t.valid then
    print(t.kind, t.name, t.distance)   --> door  Door  1.38
end

name: decode
summary: Parses a JSON string.
description: Parses JSON into Open77's bounded Lua value model. Invalid JSON returns `nil, "invalid_json"`; decoded objects and arrays contain only supported scalar/table values.

name: encode
summary: Serialises a Lua value to JSON.
description: Serializes a supported Lua value to JSON using the same bounded representation used by events, exports and WebUI. Functions, userdata, cycles and unsupported table shapes return `nil, reason`.

name: clear
summary: Clears this resource's keys matching a prefix.
description: Atomically removes every key matching an optional prefix from the calling resource's current-server store and returns the removal count. An empty prefix clears only that resource namespace.

name: compareAndSet
summary: Atomically changes a key when its typed value matches.
description: Atomically replaces a key only when its typed value exactly matches the expected value. Nil expected means the key must be absent; nil replacement deletes after a successful comparison.

name: delete
summary: Deletes one persistent key.
description: Atomically deletes one key from the current resource store and returns whether it existed. Deleting a missing key succeeds with false.
returns: true when removed, false when absent

name: find
summary: Finds typed entries by sorted key prefix.
description: Performs a sorted prefix search in the current resource store and returns bounded `{key, value, type}` records. The default result limit is 256 and the hard limit is 4096.
returns: array of { key, value, type }, or nil

name: get
summary: Reads one typed persistent value.
description: Reads a typed value from the current connection-address and resource namespace. Missing keys return the optional default (or nil) and are distinct from storage errors, which return `nil, reason`.

name: has
summary: Checks whether a persistent key exists.
description: Checks whether a key exists in the calling resource's current-server store without exposing its value or any other resource namespace.

name: increment
summary: Atomically increments a numeric key.
description: Atomically creates or increments a numeric key. Integer arithmetic remains 64-bit and rejects overflow; mixed/floating arithmetic rejects non-finite results.

name: keys
summary: Lists sorted keys matching a prefix.
description: Returns only the sorted keys matching an optional prefix in the current resource store. It is a bounded index query and cannot enumerate another package or connection address.

name: set
summary: Persists one typed value for this server address and resource.
description: Atomically persists a string, signed integer, finite number or boolean under the current connection address and resource. Keys/values and the 1 MiB resource quota are validated before the old file is replaced.

name: setIfAbsent
summary: Stores a value only when its key is missing.
description: Redis-style SETNX for the current resource namespace: atomically stores the typed value only when the key is missing and reports whether insertion occurred.

name: stats
summary: Returns this resource store's usage and quotas.
description: Returns this resource's entry/byte usage and enforced quotas together with the active address/resource scope. It exposes no keys or usage belonging to other resources.

name: acceptPickup
summary: Applique localement un pickup déjà accepté par le serveur.
description: API interne appelée uniquement après `open77:loot:pickupResult`. Elle projette l'objet dans l'inventaire REDengine local; l'inventaire persistant reste une responsabilité serveur.

name: clear
summary: Supprime toutes les projections locales et leurs prompts.
description: Clears the client-side native loot projection when the caller has `world.loot`. This is intended for the authoritative loot replication package during snapshot replacement; ordinary gameplay resources should request server-owned changes instead.

name: remove
summary: Retire une projection locale de loot.
description: Removes one replicated native loot entity from this client's projection and requires `world.loot`. It does not by itself delete the server record, so gameplay code should normally use the authoritative loot package API.

name: requestPickup
summary: Demande au serveur de ramasser un drop.
description: Le serveur contrôle l'existence, le routing bucket et la distance calculée depuis son dernier snapshot du joueur.
returns: true si la requête réseau est partie

name: setAuthorityEnabled
summary: Active ou désactive la projection de loot autoritaire.
description: Réservé à `open77_loot`. Quand il est actif, les choix, conteneurs et drops vanilla sont neutralisés et les objets physiques deviennent de simples représentations du registre serveur.

name: upsert
summary: Crée ou met à jour la projection locale d'un drop serveur.
description: API interne de réplication. Demande la permission `world.loot`; un script gameplay ne doit pas inventer un drop côté client.

params.name: drop
params.type: table { id, item, quantity, position, radius, label, model, revision }

name: cancelPick
summary: Cancels this resource's outstanding native map request.
description: Requires map.control. Returns true or false, reason. The requester receives open77:map:pointPicked with status='cancelled' when a picker was active. Resource shutdown also releases its UI ownership without delivering events to its replacement instance.

name: close
summary: Closes a map session opened by this resource.
description: Requires map.control. Returns true on accepted closure, otherwise false, reason. Cannot close a user-opened map or another resource's map. Closure is asynchronous. A pending picker is cancelled.

name: getSelectedMarker
summary: Reads the marker highlighted in the vanilla map.
description: Requires map.read. Returns a marker table or nil. kind distinguishes waypoint, quest, poi, resource and unknown. Selection is not the same as the player's waypoint; highlighting a marker does not change navigation.

name: getWaypoint
summary: Reads the player's manual vanilla waypoint.
description: Returns nil (without an error) when no player waypoint is tracked. Quest, POI and Open77 resource markers are excluded. Requires map.read. The result has a string id, kind='waypoint', source='player', position={x,y,z} and revision. Errors return nil, reason; map_unavailable means the world snapshot is unavailable or stale.

name: isOpen
summary: Checks whether the vanilla world map is open.
description: Requires map.read. Returns a boolean, or nil, reason when map state is unavailable. Uses native map controller lifecycle callbacks.

name: open
summary: Opens the vanilla map, optionally focused on a world location.
description: Requires map.control. options.position={x,y,z} optionally focuses the map. Returns requestId, or nil, reason. Acceptance is asynchronous; observe open77:map:opened or open77:map:requestFailed. Respects game UI restrictions and exclusive ownership; map_busy means another map session exists.

name: pickPoint
summary: Lets the player select a native map point without travel.
description: Requires map.control. Optional position={x,y,z} and timeoutMilliseconds (1000..300000, default 60000). Returns requestId or nil, reason. open77:map:pointPicked is delivered only to the requesting resource, with requestId, status, position and marker. Use the vanilla waypoint gesture to select. Fast travel, taxi confirmation and Open77 admin map teleport are suppressed during the picker.

name: state
summary: Reads a coherent native map snapshot.
description: Requires map.read. Returns open, picking, waypoint, selectedMarker, revision and sampleAgeMs, or nil, reason. Read this on resource startup before subscribing to change events; no historical placement event is synthesized.

name: clear
summary: Removes every 3D marker owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.markers`; other resources are unaffected.

name: create
summary: Creates a resource-owned 3D world marker.
description: Requires `world.markers`. Options require `position` and accept `shape`, `style`, `radius`, `maxDistance`, `minDistance`, and `visible`. The returned decimal-string handle preserves its full 64-bit identity.

name: list
summary: Lists the calling resource's 3D markers.
description: Requires `world.markers`. Each snapshot includes its requested definition and whether the native renderer currently presents it.
returns: array of { id, shape, style, radius, maxDistance, minDistance, visible, rendered, position }, or nil

name: remove
summary: Removes one resource-owned 3D marker.
description: Requires `world.markers`.

name: update
summary: Patches a resource-owned 3D marker.
description: Requires `world.markers`. Only supplied fields are changed, and ownership prevents mutation of another resource's marker.

name: knockdown
summary: Queue an owned native reaction on an exact local body.
description: Requires player.motion.project. entity is a local registry handle (1 for the owner), not a network player ID. Direction is normalized; distance is0..6 m and the local owner must be alive, ready, on foot and grounded. Returns an owned request ID. Owner phase starts pending, then active after two valid consecutive native-down observations within1.5s. Remote projection starts its native action immediately. No damage, teleport or server authority is granted.
example:
local request, err = Open77.motion.knockdown(1, 0, 1, 0)
if not request then print(err); return end
print(Open77.motion.state(request))

name: state
summary: Read the phase of this resource's native reaction.
description: Requires player.motion.project. Phases include pending, active and recovering; an expired/unknown/foreign ID returns nil, reason. active is a native PSM observation for the owner, not proof of physical displacement or the observer rendering. The support resource waits for active before acknowledging server motion.
example:
local phase, err = Open77.motion.state(request)
if not phase then print(err) else print(phase) end

name: stop
summary: Request cleanup of this resource's native reaction.
description: Requires player.motion.project. Pending cancellation is latched so cleanup retries cannot later activate it. Cancellation removes the owned status/action but may leave native momentum and get-up in progress. It does not instantly freeze velocity, revive a player, or cancel another resource's request.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.motion.stop(request)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: clear
summary: Removes every nameplate override owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`; other owners are unaffected.

name: remove
summary: Removes the calling resource's nameplate override for one player.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`.

name: render
summary: Draws remote-player nameplates natively, with no WebUI surface at all.
description:
Requires `ui.nameplates`. `stream` had already taken Lua off the per-frame path, and plates still trailed the world: what was left is the CEF chain itself -- IPC, a page repaint on the page's own timer, an offscreen raster, a shared-texture handoff, then the composite -- and every stage buffers. `render(true)` draws the plate in the frame that presents it, from a projection taken on that same frame, so there is nothing left to buffer and no page to create.

Guard the call rather than invoking it bare: a client older than the native drawer has no `render` at all, and indexing nil takes the whole resource down instead of falling back. `Open77.nameplates.render ~= nil and Open77.nameplates.render(true)` is the shipped form, with `stream(page)` and then a `Wait(33)` poll loop as the two fallbacks.

`render(false)` stops it. The drawer is released on stop, reload and world exit anyway, but asking explicitly is what keeps a reload from leaving one frame painted. `Open77.nameplates.set` gains `showDistance` on this path; `label`, `color` and `maxDistance` apply to every path.
returns: true when the plugin is drawing them, otherwise false

name: set
summary: Creates or updates the calling resource's nameplate override for a remote player.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Options accept `label`, `color`, `maxDistance`, and `visible`. Overrides are owner-scoped and cleaned up with the resource.

name: setTalking
summary: Shows or clears the native speaker icon on one remote player's nameplate.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Talking assertions are owner-scoped and automatically released on stop; several voice/HUD resources may assert the same player without racing. The integrated voice package drives this from authenticated native talker state.

name: snapshot
summary: Returns the currently rendered remote-player nameplates.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Screen coordinates and distance describe the most recent presentation snapshot.
returns: array of { id, label, color, x, y, distance }, or nil

name: stopStream
summary: Stops the calling resource's native nameplate stream.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Stopping a stream that does not exist succeeds, so teardown is idempotent. The stream is also dropped automatically on stop, reload, world exit, and when its page is destroyed.

name: stream
summary: Streams the native nameplate projection to a page, once per game frame.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates` and a WebUI page this resource owns. The projection was always native and always correct; relaying it from a Lua timer is what made plates lag and freeze. This publishes the same `nameplates:update` event with the same `{ players = { { id, label, color, x, y, distance } } }` payload, so an existing page needs no change and the resource can delete its `Wait(33)` loop. An identical frame is not re-sent.

name: emitServer
summary: Sends an event to the server.
description: Alias of `TriggerServerEvent`: sends a bounded, serializable event payload to the authenticated server session. The current resource must declare `network.events`.

name: on
summary: Listens for an event coming from the server.
description: Registers an authenticated incoming server event and its callback for the current resource generation. It is the namespaced equivalent of `RegisterNetEvent` and requires `network.events`.

name: catalog
summary: The catalog as of the last refresh.
description: Reads a snapshot: refreshing is asynchronous, so call `refresh`, then `catalog` a beat later.

name: connect
summary: Joins an Open77 server.
description: Starts a connection to the supplied Open77 server endpoint using the current identity and resource pipeline. It requires `network.client`; success means the request was accepted, while connection progress and errors are observed through `status()`.
returns: true when the request is accepted
example: local ok, reason = Open77.network.connect("127.0.0.1:11778", "Player")

name: disconnect
summary: Leaves the current server.
description: Requests an orderly disconnect with an optional diagnostic reason. It returns after queuing teardown; the session phase in `status()` is the authoritative view of when cleanup has completed.

name: identity
summary: Reads the local Master-backed identity profile state.
description: Returns the durable user id, current display name, registration state, and asynchronous update phase. The private key is never exposed. This bridge exists for the trusted local server browser; server-downloaded resources should use the verified player APIs instead.
returns: table { phase, generation, userId, displayName, error, registered }, or nil

name: identityUpdate
summary: Requests a signed username update from the Master.
description: Queues the HTTP enrollment on the networking worker and returns immediately. Poll `identity()` until the matching generation becomes `ready` or `failed`. The backend is deliberately available only to the trusted system server-browser resource and refuses updates during a live session.

name: refresh
summary: Asks the directory for the server catalog again.
description: Starts a master-server catalog refresh for the supplied URL and requires `network.client`. The call only accepts the request; use `catalog()` to inspect generation, phase, HTTP status, body and error.

name: status
summary: State of the network session.
description: Returns the current client session snapshot: phase, endpoint, authenticated player identity, routing bucket, rates, server time, ping and downloaded resource-set metadata. Reading it does not initiate a connection or wait for a phase change.
returns: table { phase, endpoint, playerId, routingBucket, ping, error }

name: all
summary: Lists server-owned NPCs currently known by this client.
description: Canonical creation, tasks, health and removal are server-only; see wiki/npcs.md.

name: currentTask
summary: Returns the canonical active task ID for an NPC.
description: Returns the last Open77 NPC task snapshot currently presented for a network NPC. It requires `npcs.read`; task state is ephemeral and can disappear when the NPC leaves the streaming set.

name: entity
summary: Returns the ephemeral local Open77 entity handle for an NPC projection.
description: Returns nil before readiness and after stream-out. Never cache this handle across lifecycle changes.

name: get
summary: Reads one server-owned NPC currently known by this client.
