description: Read-only and guarded by npcs.read. The snapshot includes the exact Character record; template is the legacy alias or 'record' for direct spawns. The local entity handle is generation-checked and becomes invalid after stream-out. Observe onNpcReady/onNpcSpawnFailed for asynchronous projection readiness; see wiki/npcs.md.

name: isStreamedIn
summary: Whether an NPC projection is attached and ready locally.
description: Reports whether a network NPC currently has a live client proxy in this player's streaming scope. It does not request streaming or prove that the server NPC record no longer exists.

name: applyPolicy
summary: Applies a third-person policy received from the server.
description: `disabled`, `allowed`, `default` or `forced`, with the pinned perspective for `forced` (a pin with nothing pinned is refused rather than quietly becoming first person). Requires the `perspective.policy` permission -- not because it exposes anything, since all of this is client-local presentation, but because it is the one call that can take the choice away from the player. It deliberately cannot express the bridge's fifth value, `lab`, which disengages the arbiter entirely: a server able to reach that could leave a client with nothing governing the camera. The bundled `open77_perspective` resource is the intended caller, on receipt of `open77:perspective:policy`.

name: get
summary: Returns the perspective actually in force.
description: `fpp` or `tps`, read from the committed camera owner rather than from the request -- intention is not evidence, which is the same rule `camera.state` had to learn. An engine-owned view (a vehicle camera, a cutscene) reads `fpp`, because that is what the player sees; `Open77.perspective.state().camera` keeps the distinction.

name: set
summary: Asks the perspective arbiter for first or third person.
description: Records the local player's standing request. It is a REQUEST, not a switch: the perspective arbiter coordinates camera, body, input, weapon, effects and audio. Native vehicle/workspot/death/photo-mode safety and server policy take priority; a server-policy refusal is reported as `refused_by_policy` while remembering the request. A temporary resource lock created by setThirdPerson(enabled, true) is different: it refuses an opposing request without changing the pre-lock preference, and does not record a same-view request either. Accepts `fpp`/`first`/`1` and `tps`/`tpp`/`third`/`3`. Use setThirdPerson for a boolean switch or resource-owned lock and configureThirdPerson for camera style. Do not bypass the arbiter with legacy camera.thirdPerson, which changes only the camera owner.
example:
-- Third person on foot when the player joins; the arbiter still decides
AddEventHandler("onClientResourceStart", function(name)
    if name == GetCurrentResourceName() then Open77.perspective.set("tps") end
end)

name: state
summary: Reports the whole perspective decision.
description: Client-only read; no permission required. Returns mode, requested, requestExpressed, policy, forced, resourceForced (boolean), resourcePerspective (tps/fpp/none), allowed, engaged, aiming, available, settled, transition, reason, rule, tier, the six owners (camera, body, input, weapon, effects, audio), violations, unsupportedChecks, slideFrames, slideLifted, unsupportedFires and unsupportedSource. resourceForced/resourcePerspective describe a requested local resource lock, not guaranteed ownership of a native vehicle or cutscene camera: inspect mode, camera, reason and settled for the effective view. allowed is false under a disabled/forced server policy or while a resource lock exists; an active resource lock reports reason/rule `resource_forced`. violations counts ticks where the arbiter detected conflicting body/weapon ownership; unsupported fields are diagnostic gate counters. Reads work during a live session and may return nil with `perspective_unavailable_on_this_host` if unsupported.
example:
-- Grey out the "toggle view" button when the server forbids it
local state = Open77.perspective.state()
toggleButton.enabled = state and state.allowed

name: toggle
summary: Flips the standing request and returns the new mode.
description: Flips the REQUEST, not the effective view. Native vehicle cameras keep their own rules regardless of the standing on-foot preference. For a player who has never expressed a preference, the effective view is inverted so the first press does not appear to do nothing. A temporary resource lock from setThirdPerson(enabled, true) blocks an opposing toggle and preserves the pre-lock preference; server policy and native-camera safety still take priority. Returns the new fpp/tps request on acceptance, or nil and a refusal reason.
example:
-- V flips between first and third person
RegisterKeyMapping("toggle_view", "Toggle view", "V", function()
    local mode = Open77.perspective.toggle()
    if mode then Open77.hud.notify(mode == "tps" and "Third person" or "First person") end
end)

name: close
summary: Closes Cyberpunk's native photo mode.
description: Calls the native photo-mode deactivation routine. The operation is idempotent when photo mode is already inactive.
example: Open77.photoMode.close()

name: isActive
summary: Reports whether REDengine photo mode is active.
description: Reads `gamePhotoModeSystem::IsPhotoModeActive`; it reports engine state rather than remembering the last Lua request.

name: open
summary: Opens Cyberpunk's native photo mode.
description: This is the sole supported activation path while Open77 is loaded. The native plugin refuses the stock keyboard/controller activation entry, then this call invokes the retained original REDengine implementation directly. It is idempotent when already active; REDengine can still refuse contexts in which photo mode is unavailable.
example: local ok, reason = Open77.photoMode.open()

name: setEnabled
summary: Opens or closes the native photo mode.
description: Equivalent to `open()` for true and `close()` for false. This controls one client-local engine state and is not a resource-owned lease.

name: allHealthStates
summary: Lists all replicated player health snapshots known to the client.
description: Requires `players.life.read`; returns an empty array when unavailable.

name: allLifeStates
summary: Lists all replicated canonical player life states known to the client.
description: Requires `players.life.read`; returns an empty array when unavailable.

name: getHealthState
summary: Reads one replicated player health snapshot.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. Omit `playerId` for the local player.
returns: table { playerId, revision, health, maxHealth, armor, godMode, lastAttacker, lastDamage, lastAttackKind, lastBodyPart, lastHitDirection }, or nil

name: getLifeState
summary: Reads the canonical replicated life state of one player.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. Omit `playerId` for the local session player.

name: getLocalDeathContext
summary: Reads the local player's replicated death context.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. The snapshot includes phase, cause, killer, weapon, position, yaw, impulse, revision and grace duration.

name: getVehicleSeat
summary: Reads a replicated player's canonical vehicle-seat assignment.
description: Alias of `Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat`, exposed under the player namespace. Requires `vehicles.read`; omitting `playerId` selects the local player.

name: isDead
summary: Whether a player is canonically dead or awaiting revive/respawn.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. Omit `playerId` for the local player. Unknown or unavailable states return false.

name: clear
summary: Removes every local prop this resource created.
description: Called automatically when the resource stops or reloads, so a reloading gamemode never leaves orphaned decorations behind. It never touches another resource's props, nor server-owned ones.

name: create
summary: Creates a local, decorative prop owned by this resource.
description: Requires `world.props`. This is the **client** meaning of the name: the prop is never replicated and never visible to anyone else -- a placement ghost, a build cursor, a preview being dragged. It is charged against this resource's quota and released when the resource stops. The identically-named *server* function mints an authoritative, replicated prop instead; the two `Open77` tables are different objects on different machines.

params.name: options
params.type: table { model, position, yaw?, scale?, appearance?, kind?, physics?, collision?, visible?, light? }

name: list
summary: Local props this resource owns, with what the renderer did with each.
description: Each entry carries the model, kind, physics, transform, scale, the back-end that drew it, and whether it rendered or failed. Scoped to the caller: it deliberately excludes server-owned props, which belong to the session rather than to any resource, so asking a resource-scoped question about them would return an empty table and read as "no props" rather than "wrong question". Use the `open77_props` resource's `all` export for those.

name: nearest
summary: Finds the nearest local prop owned by this resource.
description: Requires `world.props`. Searches only the calling resource's local prop set, using a 10 metre default radius. A non-positive or non-finite radius is rejected; use `list` when an unbounded set is intended.
returns: prop snapshot and distance, or nil

name: project
summary: Upserts a server-owned prop into the world, keyed by the server id.
description: What the bundled `open77_props` projection resource drives; not the way a gamemode places objects. Because the native layer is keyed by the server's own id, a prop that only moved is transformed in place rather than destroyed and rebuilt, which is what stops it visibly popping. Projected props are owned by the session, survive a resource reload, and are not charged against any resource's quota.

name: remove
summary: Removes a local prop this resource owns.
description: Removing a prop that is already gone succeeds: the caller asked for it not to be there, and it is not there. Another resource's prop answers `owned_by_another_resource`.

name: setTransform
summary: Moves a local prop to a position and yaw.
description: The one mutation the engine accepts on a live entity, so it never respawns and never pops. Scale is deliberately not part of it: scale is read when the render proxy is built, so it goes through `update` and costs a respawn.

name: unproject
summary: Stops projecting one server-owned prop.
description: Succeeds when the prop is already absent: the server is saying stop showing something, and it is not being shown.

name: unprojectAll
summary: Stops projecting every server-owned prop.
description: Used on disconnect and when the projection resource restarts, so a stale world never survives into a new session.

name: update
summary: Patches a local prop this resource owns.
description: Only the fields present in the patch are taken. Changing anything the render proxy reads when it is built -- model, scale, kind, physics, collision, visibility or the light parameters -- respawns the underlying entity rather than mutating it, because the engine offers no in-place path for those. Use `setTransform` to move a prop without that cost.

name: setBody
summary: Project a captured body onto a network player proxy.
description: Requires puppets.present. playerId is a network player ID; body={family,groups}, or false to clear the remote body. Uses asynchronous native dressing; true means acceptance, not a fully rendered proxy. Use the appearance service to distribute authoritative records and preserve wardrobe ownership.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.puppets.setBody(playerId, capturedBody)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: setSlot
summary: Project one remote equipment-slot override.
description: Requires puppets.present. playerId is a network player ID. record is a TweakDB record string (up to160 bytes), false for explicitly empty, or nil for the native default. Do not confuse nil and false when restoring a clothing snapshot. Native dressing is asynchronous; this is not durable inventory ownership.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.puppets.setSlot(playerId, "OuterChest", false)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: setWardrobe
summary: Project a remote wardrobe snapshot.
description: Requires puppets.present. snapshot={active=integer,outfits={[outfitId]={[slot]=recordOrFalse}}}. false means an explicitly empty slot. Network player IDs and native wardrobe IDs are different namespaces. This is asynchronous presentation; the server wardrobe service remains the durable source of truth.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.puppets.setWardrobe(playerId, wardrobeSnapshot)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: generation
summary: Generation number, incremented on every reload.
description: With no argument, returns the current resource generation. Pass a resource name to inspect that resource, or receive nil when it is missing.

name: hasPermission
summary: Whether the resource holds this permission.
description: Checks whether the current resource manifest grants an exact Open77 capability. It is a read-only convenience check; native APIs still enforce their own permission and must handle refusal results.

name: name
summary: Name of the current resource.
description: Returns the current resource's immutable manifest name. This is equivalent to `GetCurrentResourceName()` and remains stable for the lifetime of the resource definition.

name: readFile
summary: Reads a file from the resource, within its declared allowlist.
description: Reads a file declared by the current resource manifest through a safe relative path. Undeclared files, traversal, oversized content and host filesystem paths are rejected.

name: state
summary: State of a resource.
description: Returns the lifecycle state known for a resource name, or for the current resource when omitted. It is an immediate snapshot and does not wait for dependencies or mutate lifecycle state.

name: version
summary: Version declared in `open77.lua`.
description: Returns the version string declared by the current resource manifest. It is package metadata and is unrelated to the Open77 runtime or Lua interpreter version.

name: luaVersion
summary: Embedded Lua version.
description: Returns the embedded Lua interpreter version used by this resource VM. Use it for diagnostics or compatibility checks, not to infer the Open77 build version.

name: version
summary: Open77 version.
description: Returns the Open77 scripting runtime version exposed to resources. This describes the host API and is distinct from both the resource manifest version and game build.

name: cancel
summary: Cancels an owned native transition and restores the image immediately.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Ownership includes resource generation and host instance. Never clears a native game fade that has taken over. Emits open77:screen:cancelled with reason=requested on success.

name: catalog
summary: Lists supported native screen transition presets and backend availability.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Current preset is fade, with backend=native_quest_fade, available, color, maxDurationMs, maxHoldMs and maxTimeoutMs. Availability verifies this executable's guarded native entry, not whether a world is ready or another fade is busy. Glitch remains unsupported.

name: fadeIn
summary: Returns the image for this resource's active native fade.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. options.durationMs is 0..10000 (default 500). Can reverse an outgoing fade; does not extend the safety deadline. Rejects another owner, stale generation or an already-running return. Observe open77:screen:finished for native completion.

name: fadeOut
summary: Applies a native black or color-tinted quest fade (colored rendering is engine-controlled).
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Returns an owned string ID, not completion. Options: durationMs (0..10000, default 500), color={r,g,b,a=255}, timeoutMs (1000..60000, default at least 15000). Wait for open77:screen:black or covered, then call fadeIn or cancel. Resource cleanup and a bounded real-time deadline restore the image. See the Native screen transitions guide.

name: state
summary: Reads this resource generation's active or recent native transition.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Returns id, generation, phase, reason, backend, timing, automatic, elapsedMs, remainingMs, timeoutMs, black and color. remainingMs is the native fade timer, not hold time; native-state completion is not a GPU fence or streaming-complete signal. History is bounded to 64 global entries and removed on resource release.

name: transition
summary: Runs a native fade, bounded hold and return sequence.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Supported preset: fade. Options: durationMs=500, holdMs=250, fadeInMs=500, timeoutMs and opaque RGB color. Durations are integer milliseconds; hold is 0..30000, fades 0..10000. Only one active owner; vanilla requests retain priority. No teleport or network mutation. Glitch is not yet a supported preset.

name: characterBootstrap
summary: Reads the current character-bootstrap state.
description: Returns the current client-local character bootstrap projection as phase, body family, error and generation. The table is a snapshot; polling it does not advance the transaction.

name: failCharacterBootstrap
summary: Marks character bootstrap as failed.
description: Marks the active client-local character bootstrap as failed with an optional bounded diagnostic reason. It requires player.appearance.edit and does not disconnect the network session.

name: launcherContext
summary: What the launcher told this game process at boot.
description: Returns a table { connectEndpoint, master, serverId, modsDigest, launched } read once from the environment the OPEN//77 launcher sets when it starts the game (OP77_CONNECT, OP77_CONNECT_MASTER, OP77_WORLD_SERVER, OP77_WORLD_MODS_DIGEST), every value validated against a strict alphabet. All strings are empty and `launched` is false when the game was started without the launcher (Steam, GOG, a shortcut): that is a state, not an error. `modsDigest` is the SHA-256 of the required-mod set the launcher installed for the world it booted into, the same digest the master relays as `requiredModsDigest` in the catalogue, so the shell can decide whether this boot can join a world without a relaunch. Returns nil plus a reason only when no game backend is attached.

name: loadPristine
summary: Loads the local development world from Open77's bundled pristine save.
description: No network session is armed by this operation.

name: loadScreen
summary: Describes the connected server's declared loading screen.
description: Returns availability and the server name so the trusted shell can choose the verified server page or its built-in fallback. This function does not create the WebUI surface; the shell uses `WebUI.create({ loadScreen = true })` for that.

name: openSettings
summary: Opens the game's own settings screen without exposing the pause menu.
description: Requests the client-side Open77 settings interface. It only changes local presentation and does not modify server configuration or another player's settings.

name: quitGame
summary: Exits Cyberpunk 2077 to the desktop.
description: The vanilla exit path, reached through the script bridge rather than by terminating the process: the request is ENQUEUED and runs inside the script frame the bridge loop already owns, because a native call into script without a frame kills the process outright. Fails with `script_bridge_not_attached` before the bridge is up, `queue_full` if the bridge queue is saturated, and `game_unavailable_on_this_host` on a host with no game backend. Intended for the trusted pause surface -- `open77_pause` is the only caller -- and not for gameplay code: quitting a session is `Open77.network.disconnect`, which walks the engine back to the main menu instead of closing the game.

name: relaunchViaLauncher
summary: Hands the player to the launcher for a world this boot cannot serve.
description: Opens `open77://connect?server=<serverId>&endpoint=<host:port>&relaunch=<pid>` through the OS protocol handler the OPEN//77 launcher registers. The launcher waits for this process to exit, installs the world's required mods into its profile and starts the game again with an auto-connect to the endpoint. Nothing here terminates the game: the caller quits (Open77.session.quitGame) once this returned true, so a missing launcher is reported instead of leaving the player at the desktop. Both arguments are validated (a GUID-shaped server id, a host:port endpoint) and only that one scheme and query shape can ever be launched, so a resource cannot turn this into a generic open-URL or run-program primitive. Returns true, or false plus a reason: invalid_server_id, invalid_endpoint, launcher_not_registered (no handler for the open77 scheme on this machine), launcher_launch_failed:<code>.

name: requestCharacterCreator
summary: Requests the native character creator.
description: Requests the native character creator for the active bootstrap transaction. It requires player.appearance.edit and returns a stable failure when the game backend cannot accept the request.

name: resetCharacterBootstrap
summary: Resets the local character-bootstrap transaction.
description: Clears the client-local character bootstrap transaction so a fresh bootstrap can begin. It does not delete a server character or change another player's state.

name: resolveCharacterBootstrap
summary: Completes bootstrap with a selected body family.
description: Completes the active bootstrap with the validated female or male body family. It requires player.appearance.edit and only updates the local bootstrap backend.

name: setMenuReady
summary: Declares that this resource is able to serve the pause menu.
description: The escape key is only intercepted while this is true. A resource that fails to start therefore leaves the game's own menu reachable, rather than stranding the player with none.

name: takeCharacterCreatorResult
summary: Consumes the pending character-creator result.
description: Consumes the pending native character-creator result once and returns its serialized payload, or nil when no result is ready. It requires player.appearance.edit.

name: request
summary: Asks the script bridge to list the variables of a group.
description: Asynchronous: request, then read with `values` a beat later.

name: set
summary: Writes a settings variable.
description: Submits one local Open77 setting change through the settings backend. The key, value type and published bounds are validated; use `values()` to read the resulting projection.

name: values
summary: The variables as the script last reported them.
description: Returns a snapshot of the settings currently published by the client backend. The returned table is a copy and modifying it does not apply changes.
returns: table of { name, value, minimum, maximum, step }

name: clear
summary: Stops every SFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`; VFX and other resource owners are unaffected.

name: list
summary: Lists active SFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`.
returns: array of { id, kind, name, entity, remaining }, or nil

name: play
summary: Starts resource-owned spatial audio on an entity.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Options accept `entity`, `emitter`, `tag`, `seekTime`, `duration`, and `unique`; omitting `entity` uses the local player.

name: stop
summary: Stops one SFX handle owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`. REDengine stops audio by event name, so identical simultaneous events on one entity may share stop behavior.

name: get
summary: Reads the canonical health and stamina state for one player.
description: Requires `players.stats.read` (or the legacy `players.life.read`). Omit `playerId` for the local player. Returns the same combined shape as the server API, including both point pools, maximums, fractions, regeneration flags/rates, armor, god mode, damage attribution and revisions. Client resources cannot mutate these server-owned values.

name: getHealth
summary: Reads one player's canonical health pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.read` (or `players.life.read`). Omit `playerId` for the local player. The table contains `value/current`, `maximum/max`, `fraction`, `percentage`, `regenEnabled`, `regenPerSecond` and `regenerating`.

name: getStamina
summary: Reads one player's canonical stamina pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.read` (or `players.life.read`). Omit `playerId` for the local player. The table contains `value/current`, `maximum/max`, `fraction`, `percentage`, `regenEnabled`, `regenPerSecond` and `regenerating`.

name: health
summary: Alias of `Open77.stats.getHealth`.
description: Reads the replicated server-owned health pool. This alias has exactly the same permission, optional player id and return shape as `getHealth`.

name: stamina
summary: Alias of `Open77.stats.getStamina`.
description: Reads the replicated server-owned stamina pool. This alias has exactly the same permission, optional player id and return shape as `getStamina`.

name: monotonic
summary: Monotonic clock, in seconds.
description: Never goes backwards, unlike wall-clock time: this is the one to measure a duration with. Multiply by 1000 only when an API explicitly expects milliseconds.

name: isMapPick
summary: Whether the world-map double-click travel gesture is armed.
description: Returns whether this client has the world-map double-click travel gesture armed. It requires `player.travel` and reports false when the permission or native bridge is unavailable. This is only local input state: it neither teleports the player nor bypasses the ACL check performed by the server command that consumes a picked point.

name: isNoclip
summary: Whether local-player noclip is currently active.
description: Returns false without `player.travel` or when the backend is unavailable.

name: setMapPick
summary: Arms or disarms the world-map double-click travel gesture.
description: Requires `player.travel`. This only lets the local map publish a picked world point; it moves nobody and does not bypass the ACL-checked server command that consumes the point.

name: setNoclip
summary: Enables or disables native noclip for the local player.
description: Requires `player.travel`. Multiplayer deployments should expose this only behind an ACL-checked server command.

name: setNoclipSpeed
summary: Sets the local noclip movement speed.
description: Requires `player.travel`; the value must be finite and is validated by the native backend.

name: teleport
summary: Teleports the local player directly to a world transform.
description: Requires `player.travel`. Prefer the authoritative server respawn transaction for long-distance multiplayer moves because it handles streaming and life state.

name: all
summary: Lists every vehicle currently streamed to this client.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns an empty array when permission or the projection backend is unavailable. Every entry has the exact shape returned by `Open77.vehicles.get`; server vehicles outside the client's streaming interest set are intentionally absent.

name: clearAllPerformance
summary: Drops every performance ceiling, instance and record class alike.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Intended for a gamemode teardown so a stopped resource cannot leave cars governed.

name: clearPerformance
summary: Removes one vehicle's performance ceiling.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. The vehicle falls back to its record class profile, then the default, then to untouched native behaviour.

name: clearPerformanceClass
summary: Removes a TweakDB record's performance ceiling.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Vehicles of that record fall back to the default profile, then to untouched native behaviour.

name: get
summary: Reads one streamed server-owned vehicle.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. The snapshot contains durable state (`health`, flags, the derived `locked` boolean, six door bits, four open-window bits, tyre/glass/light masks, detached panels and the 30-cell body grid), authority and occupants including durable seat-policy flags, an ephemeral generation-checked local entity handle, plus the latest drivetrain and wheel telemetry. Open windows and broken glass are separate states. Creation, repair, authoritative seat assignment and arbitrary mutation are server-only; the complete server surface is documented in `wiki/vehicles.md`.
returns: table { id, record, entity, engineEntity, revision, physicsOwner, authorityEpoch, flags, locked, health, doors, windows, tires, bodyDamage, brokenGlass, brokenLights, detachedParts, damage, speed, rpm, rpmMax, throttle, brake, steering, wheelRotation, suspensionLongitudinal, suspensionTransversal, burnout, gear, onGround, reversing, streamed, locallyOwned, occupants }, or nil

name: getActiveWeapons
summary: Lists the attached weapons selected by the driver.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Uses captured selection for the local driver and replicated selection for observers. Unknown selection returns nil, weapon_state_unavailable; a known empty selection returns an empty table.
returns: Array of weapon tables, or nil, reason
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons, reason = Open77.vehicles.getActiveWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons then print(reason); return end
for _, weapon in ipairs(weapons) do
    print("Selected mount", weapon.index, weapon.type)
end
-- An empty array means known selection with no active attached weapons.

name: getPaint
summary: Reads replicated authoritative paint for one streamed vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns the separate `applied` flag plus primary and secondary keyed RGB tables. It returns `nil` while the vehicle is unknown or not streamed; the value is read-only on the client.
returns: table { applied, primary, secondary }, or nil
example:
local paint = Open77.vehicles.getPaint(vehicleId)
if paint and paint.applied then print(paint.primary.r, paint.primary.g, paint.primary.b) end

name: getPlayerSeat
summary: Reads a replicated player's canonical vehicle-seat assignment.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Omitting `playerId` selects the local player. The result includes `playerId`, `vehicleId`, canonical `seat`, numeric `flags`, `entering`, `exiting`, `forcedEntry`, `exitLocked`, `forcedExit`, plus the current local projection's `streamed` state and ephemeral `entity` handle. It returns nil when no assignment is currently replicated.

name: getWeapon
summary: Reads one weapon mount by its stable one-based index.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. The index comes from weapon.index, not weaponId or slotId. An unattached declared mount is returned with attached=false; invalid indices are rejected.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local weapon, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeapon(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if not weapon then print(reason); return end
print(weapon.index, weapon.attached, weapon.active)

name: getWeaponAim
summary: Reads the Basilisk's captured or replicated turret inputs.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Returns yaw, pitch and source. These are graph angles in degrees relative to the chassis, not a world aim ray. Other models or unavailable state return nil, weapon_aim_unavailable.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local aim, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponAim(seat.vehicleId)
if not aim then print(reason); return end
print(aim.yaw, aim.pitch, aim.source) -- degrees relative to the chassis

name: getWeaponAmmo
summary: Reads available native ammunition counters for a mounted weapon.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Returns available, source, optional magazine/capacity/total/reserve. Ammunition is native-local-driver only; observer counters are not replicated and are omitted, never invented as zero. Counters do not establish whether a mounted weapon has infinite ammo or can fire.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local ammo, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponAmmo(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if not ammo then print(reason); return end
if ammo.available and ammo.magazine ~= nil then
    print(ammo.magazine, ammo.capacity)
else
    print("--", ammo.source) -- e.g. not_replicated for a passenger
end

name: getWeaponCount
summary: Counts weapon objects attached to a streamed vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Returns actual attached count, not declaredCount or activeCount. Zero means a known streamed vehicle with no resolved weapon objects.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local count, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponCount(seat.vehicleId)
if count == nil then print(reason); return end
print("Attached weapons:", count) -- zero is valid

name: getWeaponModel
summary: Reads the weapon mounts declared by a vehicle model.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. This is a TweakDB declaration, not proof that all weapons are attached in an appearance. Returns record, hasWeaponMounts, declaredCount and mounts.
example:
local model, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponModel("Vehicle.v_militech_basilisk")
if not model then print(reason); return end
print(model.record, model.declaredCount)
for _, mount in ipairs(model.mounts) do
    print(mount.index, mount.record, mount.slot, mount.type)
end

name: getWeaponState
summary: Reads one coherent mounted-weapon snapshot.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Uses a canonical network vehicle ID. Includes declared mounts, attached/active counts, selection mask, local-driver flag and available native ammo/heat. Local reads are cached for at most 100 ms.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if seat then
    local state, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponState(seat.vehicleId)
    if state then print(state.attachedCount, state.activeCount) end
end

name: getWeaponType
summary: Reads a mounted weapon's stable category.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Categories: machine_gun, cannon, missile, countermeasure, unknown. Native itemType, when available, is a separate field in getWeapon.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local category, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponType(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if not category then print(reason); return end
print(category) -- machine_gun, cannon, missile, countermeasure or unknown

name: getWeapons
summary: Lists the weapon objects actually attached to a streamed vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. The returned array is dense but each weapon.index preserves its one-based position in the model mount list. Do not use the array position as the mount index.
returns: Array of weapon tables, or nil, reason
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons then print(reason); return end
for _, weapon in ipairs(weapons) do
    print(weapon.index, weapon.type, weapon.slot)
end

name: honk
summary: Alias of `Open77.vehicles.triggerHorn`.
description: Requires `vehicles.control` and local physics ownership. Duration is bounded to 100..2000 ms and defaults to 250 ms.

name: isArmed
summary: Checks whether a streamed vehicle actually has attached weapons.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Counts resolved weapon objects, not the model's inherited mount declarations. An unstreamed vehicle returns nil, vehicle_not_streamed.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local armed, reason = Open77.vehicles.isArmed(seat.vehicleId)
if armed == nil then print(reason); return end
print(armed and "Attached weapons found" or "No attached weapons")

name: isDoorOpen
summary: Reads a canonical vehicle door, trunk, or hood state.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Accepts index 0..5, a standard camelCase/snake_case name, or a `Open77.vehicles.doors` constant. This reads the replicated reversible opening mask.
returns: boolean, or nil when denied, unavailable, or unknown

name: isLocked
summary: Reads a vehicle's replicated entry-lock state.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns the durable server-authoritative lock for a streamed vehicle. This is the vehicle entry lock, not the per-occupant exit lock and not the client-side grid control lock.
returns: boolean, or nil when the vehicle is unknown

name: isPlayerExitLocked
summary: Reports the replicated exit-lock policy for a player.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Omitting `playerId` selects the local player. Returns nil when the player has no replicated seat assignment; otherwise returns the canonical `exitLocked` boolean.

name: isWeaponActive
summary: Checks whether the driver selected a particular attached mount.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Selection is not a firing event or a guarantee of native mesh deployment. Unknown selection is an explicit error.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local active, reason = Open77.vehicles.isWeaponActive(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if active == nil then print(reason); return end
print(active and "Selected" or "Not selected") -- not a firing flag

name: isWindowOpen
summary: Reads a canonical openable side-window state.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Windows use indexes 0..3 and names `frontLeft`, `frontRight`, `backLeft`, and `backRight`. This does not report shattered glass; inspect `brokenGlass` or `damage.glass` in the vehicle snapshot for that.
returns: boolean, or nil when denied, unavailable, or unknown

name: modelHasWeaponMounts
summary: Checks whether a vehicle model declares any weapon mounts.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. A valid unarmed model returns false; an unknown model returns nil. Inherited mounts do not guarantee a usable armed vehicle.
example:
local declared, reason = Open77.vehicles.modelHasWeaponMounts("Vehicle.v_militech_basilisk")
if declared == nil then print(reason); return end
print(declared and "Model declares mounts" or "No declared mounts")
-- Declarations alone do not prove weapons are attached to a live vehicle.

name: ratedTopSpeed
summary: Gearing rating of a vehicle's TweakDB record, in km/h.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns the speed at which the record's top gear reaches its rated maximum engine RPM, reached through `vehEngineData`. Use it to rank a roster and to pick a ceiling no car has to be slowed much to meet. It is **not** the measured terminal velocity, which torque and aerodynamic drag carry higher. Returns `nil` when the record cannot be resolved.

name: setControlLock
summary: Locks or releases a stopped vehicle's driving inputs.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. While locked, the native drive update consumes zero acceleration, zero brake/reverse and no burnout. Releasing restores REDengine's current input snapshot on the next frame; the API never teleports or clamps velocity. Use it for authoritative starting grids after the vehicle is stationary. Like the performance governor, this is client-side gamemode enforcement, not an anti-cheat boundary.

name: setFrozen
summary: Freezes or wakes a vehicle's native chassis physics.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Disables the verified REDengine vehicle physics group without changing the authority lease, player-controlled state or mounted workspot. Unlike `setControlLock`, this stops inertia, gravity and external impulses without teleporting the vehicle. Releasing restores the mask and calls the native physics wake-up path. Pair both calls for a starting grid: lock inputs then freeze; on GO thaw then unlock inputs. Unknown or not-yet-streamed vehicles fail so the resource can retry.

name: setPerformance
summary: Caps one vehicle's top speed and pickup on this client.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Cyberpunk 2077 2.31 has no speed setter, so the ceiling is applied by withdrawing driver throttle where the drive update reads it, tapered across a band so the top of the acceleration curve flattens instead of hitting a wall. The profile table takes `topSpeedKph` (0 leaves the top end alone), `taperKph` (default 12, values under 3 are refused because a narrower band makes the limiter hunt) and `accelerationScale` in (0, 1]. Precedence is instance, then record class, then default. **This is balance, not anti-cheat**: the client that simulates the vehicle applies it, and a modified client can decline to. Cleared automatically on despawn.

name: setPerformanceClass
summary: Caps every present and future vehicle spawned from one TweakDB record.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. This is the shape a roster wants: name the cars offered and the ceiling they share once, rather than tracking instances. Same profile table as `setPerformance`. A record class is overridden by an explicit per-instance profile.

name: taskPlayerEnterVehicle
summary: Presents an authorized replicated occupant with the staged entry path.
description: Requires `vehicles.presentation` and an already-authorized occupancy tuple. Uses the guarded door/workspot presentation for a live remote entry and retains a bounded instant-warp fallback. This is presentation only and never grants a seat or changes physics authority.

name: triggerHorn
summary: Sounds the horn of a locally simulated vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.control`. The vehicle must be streamed and this client must be its current physics owner. Duration is bounded to 100..2000 ms. For an arbitrary vehicle, call the authoritative server API so it can route the request to the current owner.

name: warpPlayerIntoVehicle
summary: Presents a replicated player instantly in an authoritative vehicle seat.
description: Requires `vehicles.presentation`. This is the client meaning of the name: a guarded visual operation for an existing server-owned vehicle and occupancy assignment. It does not claim the seat or physics authority. The exact `(player, vehicle, seat)` tuple must already exist in the replicated ledger or the call fails with `occupancy_mismatch`. The server runtime exposes an identically named authoritative assignment API; the two Lua states are distinct.

name: attach
summary: Attach an owned world effect to a local native body slot.
description: Requires world.effects. effectId and entity are local handles; slot is a nonempty native slot name up to128 bytes. anchor defaults to body; weaponRight uses the supported equipped weapon anchor. Missing body/slot/weapon is a refusal, not permission to bind an unrelated target. True is native attachment acceptance, not visual proof.
example:
local entity, err = Open77.vfx.resolveTarget({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)})
if not entity then print(err); return end
local ok, reason = Open77.vfx.attach(effectId, entity, "RightHand", "body")
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: catalog
summary: Returns the curated stable world-VFX aliases and cooked paths.
description: Catalog access does not start an effect. Raw cooked paths remain build-dependent even when present.
returns: table mapping alias to effect path, or nil

name: clear
summary: Stops every VFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`; SFX and other resource owners are unaffected.

name: list
summary: Lists active VFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`.
returns: array of { id, kind, name, entity, remaining }, or nil

name: play
summary: Starts a resource-owned world VFX at a fixed transform.
description: Requires `world.effects`. `options` requires `position` and accepts `orientation`, `duration`, and `ignoreTimeDilation`. The effect is released automatically with its owner.

name: playEntity
summary: Starts a resource-owned authored VFX on an entity.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Options accept `entity`, `instance`, `persistOnDetach`, `breakAllLoops`, `breakAllOnDestroy`, and `duration`; omitting `entity` targets the local player.

name: resolveTarget
summary: Resolve a typed network target to its currently streamed local handle.
description: Requires world.effects. Accepts {kind="player"|"npc"|"vehicle"|"prop",id=decimalStringOrInteger}. Returns a decimal string local registry handle (local player resolves to1), or nil, reason such as target_not_streamed. Re-resolve after stream/body changes; never send this local handle over the network.
example:
local handle, err = Open77.vfx.resolveTarget({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)})
if handle then print(handle) else print(err) end

name: setParameter
summary: Set a scalar parameter on an owned native world effect.
description: Requires world.effects. Parameter name is nonempty, at most128 bytes and contains no NUL; value must be finite. The native graph must actually expose the requested parameter. Acceptance does not guarantee visible change and does not modify authoritative gameplay.
example:
-- Only use a parameter authored by your chosen effect graph.
local ok, err = Open77.vfx.setParameter(effectId, parameterName, 0.5)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: stop
summary: Stops one VFX handle owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`.

name: update
summary: Move an owned native world effect.
description: Requires world.effects. options.position is a finite{x,y,z}; optional orientation{x,y,z,w} must be a nonzero quaternion and is normalized. Updates an existing owned world effect, not the registry target or TTL; use server attached effects for replicated lifetime.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.vfx.update(effectId, {position={x=0,y=0,z=1}})
if not ok then print(err) end

name: devices
summary: Enumerates active native voice endpoints.
description: Requires `voice.client`. `flow` is `input`, `output`, or `all`; the empty endpoint id represents the current Windows communications default.
returns: array of { id, name, flow, default, selected, available }, or nil

name: selectDevice
summary: Selects a microphone or voice output endpoint.
description: Requires `voice.client`. `flow` is `input` or `output`; an empty id follows the Windows communications default.

name: setCaptureEnabled
summary: Enables or disables native microphone capture.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Capture alone does not select recipients or bypass PTT/server policy.

name: setChannelVolume
summary: Sets local gain for a voice route/channel.
description: Requires `voice.client`. The native engine retains it for current and future streams using that route id.

name: setInputVolume
summary: Sets microphone gain.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Gain is clamped before the native capture frame is metered and encoded; the pause package persists it per server.

name: setMicrophoneTest
summary: Enables local microphone loopback.
description: Requires `voice.client`. This is a bounded local monitor and does not transmit by itself.

name: setOutputVolume
summary: Sets the global remote-voice gain.
description: Requires `voice.client`. This is local rendering policy and does not affect what any other listener hears.

name: setPlayerBlocked
summary: Locally blocks or unblocks one remote talker.
description: This affects only local playback. Use the server mute/deaf APIs for authoritative policy.

name: setPlayerVolume
summary: Sets one remote player's local playback gain.
description: Requires `voice.client`. The preference is applied to the native jitter/render path only; it cannot change server reachability.

name: setProximityDistance
summary: Requests a personal proximity-voice reach.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Queues a reliable request only; the authenticated server clamps it to the advertised minimum/maximum and republishes the canonical value in `status().proximityDistance`. Proximity remains permanently enabled unless server policy disables it; this method cannot change enabled, mute, deaf, buckets, memberships, or recipients.
returns: true when queued or already canonical, otherwise false

name: setTransmitting
summary: Sets PTT state and requested route intent.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Intent may be `proximity`, `channels`, `channel:<id>`, or `all`. `channels` selects up to four authorized speakable memberships and `all` adds proximity. The server still validates every recipient and membership.

name: setVoiceActivation
summary: Enables VAD and sets its normalized threshold.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Threshold `0` is most sensitive and `1` least sensitive. The native gate uses a short hangover, emits an explicit talkspurt end, and sends no silent talkspurt frames; held PTT may still use bounded Opus DTX.

name: status
summary: Returns one native voice capture/render snapshot.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Includes device ids, gains, input/output levels, PTT/VAD state, packet counters, active talker count, backend states, and the local canonical proximity reach. `proximityDistance` is server-confirmed; `requestedProximityDistance` and `proximityRequestPending` describe an in-flight request. The server-advertised default/minimum/maximum bounds are read-only. It never includes audio payloads.

name: talkers
summary: Lists native remote-talker playback state.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Each entry contains player id, speaking/level state, local volume/block preference, and authorized active routes.
returns: array of talker snapshots, or nil

name: activate
summary: Activates a native outfit or returns to the worn set.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Pass an outfit index; false, nil or omitted disables the active outfit. Activation does not itself prove all garment visuals have settled.

name: active
summary: Reads the active native outfit index.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns the outfit index or false when no outfit is active; false is not an error.
returns: index or false, or nil, reason

name: outfit
summary: Returns slot operations bound to a native outfit index.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Index must be an integer from 0 through 6. The result contains index and bound registry(), equip(record[, slot][, options]), unequip(slot), hide(slot) and apply(slots[, options]) functions; call them with dot syntax. registry requires read permission; mutations separately require player.equipment.edit. hide marks an outfit slot hidden, while unequip removes its override. apply false marks a hidden slot, and replace controls preservation of omitted overrides. Editing does not automatically activate the outfit.

name: activate
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.setActive`.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`; see `setActive` for template placement and asynchronous completion semantics.

name: all
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.snapshot`.
description: Requires `player.weapons.read`; results arrive asynchronously as slot-state events followed by completion.

name: assign
summary: Assigns an exact TweakDB weapon template to a standard loadout slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. `slot` is 1..3. Options are `active` (default false) and `addToInventory` (default true). The return value only confirms that the validated request was queued; listen for `open77:weapons:completed` for the state verified by REDscript.

name: holster
summary: Holsters the currently drawn right-hand weapon.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. Loadout assignments and the selected equipment-area item are unchanged; completion reports whether the right-hand slot became empty.

name: remove
summary: Removes the weapon assigned to one standard slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. This unequips the item but does not delete it from inventory. The empty slot is verified asynchronously.

name: setActive
summary: Selects and draws a standard weapon by slot or TweakDB template.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. A numeric target must already contain a weapon. A template target reuses an assigned instance or equips it first; options accept fallback `slot` 1..3 and `addToInventory` (default true). Completion is asynchronous through `open77:weapons:completed`.

name: setAmmo
summary: Sets exact spare and/or loaded ammunition for a weapon slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. `amounts` accepts integer `reserve` and `magazine` counts plus optional `activate`. At least one count is required; omitted counts are preserved. The operation verifies the shared ammo total, spare reserve, magazine, and live capacity asynchronously through `open77:weapons:completed`.

name: slots
summary: Lists the three supported standard weapon slots.
description: Requires `player.weapons.read`. Slot numbers are one-based and deliberately exclude QuickSlot grenades, WeaponHeavy items, and ArmsCW cyberware.

name: snapshot
summary: Requests the verified state of every standard weapon slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.read`. Emits one `open77:weapons:state` event per available slot and then `open77:weapons:completed`. TweakDB IDs remain opaque hexadecimal strings and are the presence authority; `record` may be empty for items equipped outside this API because shipping builds do not retain every reverse TweakDB name.

name: unequip
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.remove`.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`; the inventory instance is retained.

name: create
summary: Creates a web surface.
description:
**Creation is asynchronous.** A `show()` issued right after `create` loses the race against the `visible` flag the request carried, and the surface then never paints at all. So a surface meant to stay up is created with `visible = true`, and the page shows or hides its own content.

Valid layers: `hud`, `menu`, `modal`, `system` (needs the `webui.system` permission), `debug`.

name: default
summary: The surface declared by `web_ui_page` in the manifest.
description: Returns the auto-created WebUI page declared by `web_ui_page` in the current manifest. It returns `nil, reason` when the resource has no live default page; the handle is generation-owned and becomes stale after destroy or reload.

name: groundZ
summary: Height of the static ground below a point, by a downward ray.
description: Casts a `Static`-only ray straight down from `(x, y, fromZ)` over one kilometre and returns the Z of the first surface. Static only on purpose: a parked car or a body is not the ground. The default start height clears every rooftop in Night City. Returns nil when nothing was hit (open water, outside the world). Requires `world.query`.
returns: z (number), or nil when nothing is below
example:
local z = Open77.world.groundZ(-1460.2, 99.9)
if z then Open77.props.create({ model = "crate", position = { x = -1460.2, y = 99.9, z = z } }) end

name: nearby
summary: Every object within a radius of the local player, nearest first.
description: Exposes `Api::WorldQuery::Around`, the engine's own targeting search. It is centred on the local player because the search takes a source object, not a point: to look around somewhere else, stand there. `filter` narrows the object classes: a name, a list of names or a raw mask. Names: `player`, `puppet`, `sensor`, `device`, `other` (classes), `friendly`, `hostile`, `neutral`, `alive`, `dead`, `turnedOn`, `turnedOff`, `quickHackable` (attitude and state bits, which widen a search rather than narrow it). Absent means every class. Each hit carries `engineEntity`, the stable engine id to key on, `className`, `position` and `distance`. The first call in a session can answer `part_layout_not_proven` until something targetable has been under the crosshair once; treat it as "try again later". Radius is capped at 1000 m. Requires `world.query`.

params.name: filter
params.type: string | table of strings | number mask

returns: array of { engineEntity, className, position { x, y, z }, distance } sorted by distance, or nil
reason: permission_denied:world.query, invalid_radius, invalid_filter, world_unavailable_on_this_host, player_unavailable, part_layout_not_proven
example:
for _, hit in ipairs(Open77.world.nearby(15, { "device" }) or {}) do
  print(hit.className, hit.distance)
end

name: nearest
summary: The closest object within a radius of the local player, or nil.
description: Same search and same filter vocabulary as `Open77.world.nearby`, returning only the first hit. Requires `world.query`.

params.name: filter
params.type: string | table of strings | number mask

returns: table { engineEntity, className, position { x, y, z }, distance }, or nil
example: local door = Open77.world.nearest(5, "device")

name: raycast
summary: Traces a physics ray between two world points and returns the nearest blocking surface.
description: Runs `gameSpatialQueriesSystem::SyncRaycastByCollisionGroup`, the same native the combat and camera code use, against the `Static` and `Dynamic` collision groups and keeps the nearer hit. `options` may disable either group (`{ static = true, dynamic = false }`). The result is what the engine's trace publishes: position, surface normal, material name and distance. It carries no entity: resolve the thing you hit with `Open77.world.nearest` around the hit point. Synchronous, on the game thread, one native call per invocation; requires the `world.query` permission.
returns: table { hit, position { x, y, z }, normal { x, y, z }, material, distance } (position, normal, material and distance only when hit is true), or nil
reason: permission_denied:world.query, invalid_from, invalid_to, world_unavailable_on_this_host, or the engine status
example:
local origin = Open77.character.state().position
local target = { x = origin.x + 20, y = origin.y, z = origin.z }
local ray = Open77.world.raycast(origin, target)
if ray and ray.hit then
  print(("wall %.1f m ahead (%s)"):format(ray.distance, ray.material))
end

name: safeAreasEnabled
summary: Whether the vanilla safe-area marking is currently in effect.
description: Reads the effective safe-area state across every resource that claimed it through `Open77.world.setSafeAreas`: true when the staged interiors behave as vanilla (walk-only, weapons holstered), false while at least one running resource holds the marking off. Requires the `world.safeareas` permission. Returns nil plus a reason when the permission is missing or no game backend is attached.

name: setSafeAreas
summary: Turns the vanilla safe-area marking of staged interiors on or off for this session.
description: Vanilla marks a handful of interiors (the Afterlife, Lizzie's, Clouds) as staged, walk-only, weapons-holstered space. `setSafeAreas(false)` takes that marking off for the duration of the session, which is what makes a lobby staged in the Afterlife playable rather than a walking simulator. The claim is cooperative and owner-scoped: safe areas return once every claiming resource has released (or stopped), never because one resource asked. Requires the `world.safeareas` permission. Returns true plus the effective state across every owner, so a caller can see that another resource still holds safe areas off; false plus a reason on failure (permission_denied:world.safeareas, safe_area_backend_unavailable, invalid_safe_area_argument).
returns: effective state across owners, or reason on failure

name: destroy
summary: Destroys the surface.
description: Destroys this resource-owned browser surface, removes all of its Lua event handlers and invalidates the page handle. Resource teardown performs the same cleanup automatically.

name: hide
summary: Hides the surface.
description: Makes the owned browser surface invisible without destroying its document or handlers. Visibility is client-local and can be restored with `show()`.

name: id
summary: Numeric id of the surface.
description: Returns the opaque client-local surface id for diagnostics and host integration. It is not a network id and must not be persisted across page destruction or resource reload.

name: off
summary: Removes a handler registered with `on`.
description: Removes one WebUI callback id previously returned by `page:on`. The id is the only argument -- there is no event name parameter. It must belong to this page and the current resource generation.

name: on
summary: Listens for an event the page raised with `Open77.emit`.
description: Registers a Lua callback for an event emitted by this page's JavaScript bridge. Event names and handler counts are bounded, and the registration is automatically removed with the page or resource generation.

name: reply
summary: Answers an `invoke` call made by the page.
description: Completes a pending JavaScript request identified by its request id with a JSON-serializable Lua value. The payload is the SECOND argument and the success flag the third: `page:reply(requestId, { accepted = true })` resolves the promise, and a third argument of `false` rejects it. Success defaults to true when omitted. The payload is positional and cannot be skipped -- an absent third argument fails with `invalid_webui_reply`, though an explicit `nil` is accepted. Request ids are page-local and invalid or unsupported payloads are rejected.

name: send
summary: Sends an event to the page.
description: Sends a named event and JSON-serializable payload from Lua to this page's JavaScript runtime. This is local UI IPC, not a network event, and both event names and payloads are bounded.

name: setFocus
summary: Gives the surface focus, cursor and keyboard separately.
description: The FIRST argument is keyboard capture, not a general `focused` flag, and the second is the cursor: `page:setFocus(true, true)` takes both, `page:setFocus(false, true)` takes only the mouse. Keyboard capture is asked for separately so a page can take the mouse without depriving the game of the movement keys. The optional third argument keeps game input alive while the page holds focus and requires `webui.keep_input`; without that permission it fails with `permission_denied:webui.keep_input`.

name: show
summary: Shows the surface.
description: Avoid calling this right after `create` — see the race described in `Open77.webui.create`.

name: current
summary: Read a player's authoritative active RP playback state.
description: Requires players.animations.read. Returns the active state synchronously, or nil without an error when inactive. Fields include epoch, revision, playerId, playbackId, active, bucket, steps, loop, startedAtMs, serverTimeMs, cycle, step, elapsedMs and remainingMs. Timestamps are monotonic server time and step/cycle indices are zero-based. clientRequestId is internal correlation, not a cancellation token. State proves scheduling, not that a native clip rendered. Unlike client current(entity), this does not return a raw clip name. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: Active playback state, or nil when inactive
example:
local state, err = Open77.animations.current(playerId)
if err then print(err); return end
if state then print(state.playbackId, state.step, state.elapsedMs) end

name: get
summary: Read the definition and allowed clips of one RP profile.
description: No capability is required. Looks up an exact, case-sensitive profile ID such as smoke or phone. Returns nil without an error for an unknown profile. Use the returned clip and clips fields to construct a valid playback request instead of passing arbitrary game animation names. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: Profile table, or nil when absent
example:
local profile, err = Open77.animations.get('smoke')
if err then print(err); return end
if profile then print(profile.clip, #profile.clips) end

name: list
summary: Search the authoritative RP profile catalogue.
description: No capability is required. Returns profile definitions synchronously, not a Promise. Search is a case-insensitive substring across ID, label and category; the maximum query length is 128 characters. Empty search returns all 15 profiles and no match returns an empty array. Definitions include clip variants and rig metadata, which must not be mistaken for proof of native rendering. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
example:
local profiles, err = Open77.animations.list('social')
if not profiles then print(err); return end
for _, profile in ipairs(profiles) do print(profile.id, profile.label) end

name: play
summary: Start a server-owned, synchronized RP action on a player.
description: Requires players.animations.control. The player must be ready, alive, on foot and have a known position. The calling resource VM generation owns the action; another resource cannot replace it. Options are clip, durationMs and loop only. loop defaults to true; omitted/zero duration is indefinite when looping. With loop=false the default is 5000 ms. Nonzero durations are integers from 1000 to 600000 ms; variants must belong to the profile. Returns authoritative acceptance, not proof of native mounting. The local view temporarily uses third person. Unlike the legacy client play(entity, rawClip), this method replicates a curated profile. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.

name: sequence
summary: Schedule a server-owned sequence of RP profiles for a player.
description: Requires players.animations.control and the same readiness and ownership checks as play(). Accepts 1–16 steps with profile, optional clip and durationMs. Each step defaults to 5000 ms and must last at least 1000 ms; the total cannot exceed 600000 ms. The only sequence option is loop, default false. Durations schedule server transitions and are not measured native clip lengths. Profile switches require workspot exit/re-entry and may not blend seamlessly. Server resource stop, player death, vehicle entry, movement or bucket changes cancel the action. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.

name: stop
summary: Stop an RP action owned by the calling server resource.
description: Requires players.animations.control. Omitting playbackId stops the current action owned by this VM generation; an action owned by another resource is refused. Pass the recorded ID in delayed callbacks so an old timer cannot stop a newer action: stale IDs return stale_playback. Stopping an already inactive player succeeds. The authoritative onPlayerAnimationChanged event carries the player ID string and JSON state string; native detachment may finish asynchronously on clients. This is not the client-local stop(entity) method. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: true on success, including already inactive
example:
local playback, err = Open77.animations.play(playerId, 'smoke')
if not playback then print(err); return end
SetTimeout(10000, function()
    local stopped, reason = Open77.animations.stop(playerId, playback.playbackId)
    if not stopped then print(reason) end
end)

name: createScope
summary: Enable scoped PvP for an explicit ready roster.
description: Requires combat.scope.control. definition={bucket,players={...}} accepts2..32 unique positive player IDs currently combat-capable in that bucket; a player belongs to at most one scope. Limits64 scopes globally/8 per resource. Scope can permit PvP while global PvP is off but keeps team, life, invulnerability and Lua veto rules. Stop/disconnect/bucket changes remove ownership/participants. Creator must enforce opt-in; no automatic team or bucket change occurs.
example:
local scope, err = Open77.combat.createScope({bucket=arenaBucket,players={firstPlayer,secondPlayer}})
if not scope then print(err); return end
-- Retain scope for teardown.

name: removeScope
summary: Remove this resource's scoped PvP permission.
description: Requires combat.scope.control. Accepts the32-character scope ID returned by createScope. Does not alter global PvP or revive/teleport participants. Missing or foreign scopes fail; ordinary combat policy applies after removal.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.combat.removeScope(scopeId)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: activity
summary: Read fresh authoritative Gorilla charge activity.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returns {player,incarnation,sequence,armed,holding,charged,chargeExpired,holdAt,elapsedMs,remainingMs,maxChargeMs,definition,grade}. Null for unavailable/stale (over1500ms) body/implant activity. Values drive presentation, not an extra permission to commit damage. Hold expiry latches until release/new swing.
example:
local activity = Open77.cyberware.activity(playerId)
if activity and activity.holding then print(activity.remainingMs) end

name: bind
summary: Bind the authenticated player to a server-selected durable character.
description: Requires players.cyberware.identity. The user UUID comes from the connection; only the character key is supplied. Identity ownership is exclusive to a resource. Starts asynchronous database/native restoration; success is not readiness. Prefer the shipped appearance identity adapter and never accept an unvalidated client-selected character key.
example:
-- In a trusted identity adapter after server-side character selection:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.bind(playerId, "default")
if not result then print(err) end

name: cancel
summary: Cancel an owned installation/removal before durable commit.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. Supply the ticket from the same resource's operation. Native staging is rolled back; an already submitted storage transaction returns operation_committing and completes normally. Never refund irrevocably until the correlated operation outcome is known.
example:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.cancel(playerId, ticket)
if not result then print(err) end

name: current
summary: Read the ready durable implant record.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returned synchronously, not a Promise. Record fields are revision, arms and operationId; arms includes instanceId, definition, definitionVersion, profile, slot and the committed grade snapshot. Returns nil while loading/projecting/failed. An empty arms value means no installed implant. Temporary arena overlays do not overwrite this record. A ready record does not imply its definition provider is running.
returns: record table, or nil when not ready
example:
local record, err = Open77.cyberware.current(playerId)
if record then print(record.revision, record.arms and record.arms.definition) elseif err then print(err) end

name: define
summary: Register resource-owned Gorilla Arms grades.
description: Requires players.cyberware.define. definition={id,version,slot="arms",profile="gorilla_arms",grades={...}}. IDs use1..96 ASCII alphanumeric/_.:- characters; version positive;1..32 unique grades. Required grade fields: id,normalDamage/chargedDamage(0..300),knockbackMeters(0..6),cooldownMs(100..600000),chargeMs(100..10000). Optional normalKnockbackMeters defaults to35% of charged, maxChargeMs defaults10000 and must be>=chargeMs and<=60000; nullable normalStaminaCost/chargedStaminaCost0..300 retain native price when omitted. nonlethal/cosmetic defaultfalse; blockDamageMultiplier0..1 default0 and blockAngleDegrees0..180 default45. Stop unregisters the provider and disables its grants without deleting paid records.

name: effective
summary: Read the ready implant including an active temporary loadout.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returned synchronously, not a Promise. Record fields are revision, arms and operationId; arms includes instanceId, definition, definitionVersion, profile, slot and the committed grade snapshot. An active lease overlays arms; durable revision/operationId retain their base meaning. Pending/restoring projections return nil. Use current() for paid storage identity and effective() for ready presentation/gameplay loadout.
example:
local record = Open77.cyberware.effective(playerId)
if record and record.arms then print(record.arms.grade.id) end

name: install
summary: Stage a durable Gorilla Arms installation.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. options requires expectedRevision and operationId. Compare-and-swap and receipt storage are atomic; reuse the same ID/contents on retries. Native projection occurs before commit. Completion is asynchronous via onCyberwareOperationCompleted(playerId,ticket,encodedResult), correlated by ticket; retain the pending operation until final outcome. Rejected/failed work restores the prior paid record. Server makers own consent, costs and progression.
returns: {ok=true,ticket=string,...}; ticket may be absent on a completed idempotent replay
example:
local record = Open77.cyberware.current(playerId)
if not record then return end
local operationId, err = Open77.cyberware.newOperationId()
if not operationId then print(err); return end
local result, rejected = Open77.cyberware.install(playerId, "myrp.gorilla", "training", {
 expectedRevision=record.revision,operationId=operationId
})
if not result then print(rejected) else print(result.ticket) end

name: lease
summary: Stage a temporary implant without overwriting paid state.
description: Requires players.cyberware.temporary. options.durationMs is1000..300000, default300000. Requires a ready bound character and registered definition/grade. pending→active only after native acknowledgement. Wait for the matching onCyberwareLeaseChanged state before admitting PvP. Owner stop, body/bucket change, expiry or disconnect releases the overlay; native restoration remains asynchronous.
example:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.lease(playerId, "myrp.gorilla", "training", {durationMs=60000})
if not result then print(err); return end
-- Keep result.lease; wait for its matching active event before PvP.

name: leaseState
summary: Read a temporary loadout lease and restoration phase.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returns {id,player,phase,definition,grade,expiresAt,ticket,reason}, or nil when none exists. Phases pending/active/restoring/failed; ended is an event state, then the read becomes nil. expiresAt is server-monotonic milliseconds. Wait for nil AND current() ready before another lease.
example:
local state = Open77.cyberware.leaseState(playerId)
if state then print(state.id, state.phase) end

name: newOperationId
summary: Create an operation ID to retain across durable retries.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. Returns a32-character GUID string. Store it with the pending operation and reuse the same ID, expectedRevision and contents when retrying; generating a new ID per retry loses receipt idempotency. This does not start a transaction.
example:
local operationId, err = Open77.cyberware.newOperationId()
if not operationId then print(err); return end
-- Persist operationId with the intended mutation before submitting it.

name: releaseLease
summary: Release this resource's temporary loadout and restore paid arms.
description: Requires players.cyberware.temporary. Works during pending/active; repeated restoration requests return the same ticket. Lease id and resource owner must match. An ended event due to body loss alone is not proof of native paid restoration: wait for no lease and a ready current record.
example:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.releaseLease(playerId, leaseId)
if not result then print(err) end

name: remove
summary: Stage a durable Gorilla Arms removal.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. options requires expectedRevision and operationId. Compare-and-swap and receipt storage are atomic; reuse the same ID/contents on retries. Native projection occurs before commit. Completion is asynchronous via onCyberwareOperationCompleted(playerId,ticket,encodedResult), correlated by ticket; retain the pending operation until final outcome. Rejected/failed work restores the prior paid record. Server makers own consent, costs and progression.
returns: {ok=true,ticket=string,...}; ticket may be absent on a completed idempotent replay
example:
local record = Open77.cyberware.current(playerId)
if not record then return end
local operationId, err = Open77.cyberware.newOperationId()
if not operationId then print(err); return end
local result, rejected = Open77.cyberware.remove(playerId, {
 expectedRevision=record.revision,operationId=operationId
})
if not result then print(rejected) else print(result.ticket) end

name: unbind
summary: Release this resource's character binding and runtime grants.
description: Requires players.cyberware.identity. Does not delete durable implants. Stops current projection/temporary ownership and prevents stale acknowledgements from restoring the old grant. Another owner cannot unbind the character.
example:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.unbind(playerId)
if not result then print(err) end

name: attach
summary: Create a replicated effect bound to a typed target and native slot.
description: Requires world.effects. target={kind="player"|"npc"|"vehicle"|"prop",id=decimalStringOrInteger}; effect is an installed preset. options requires slot; optional localAnchor=body|weaponRight, localSlot, ttlMs, streamingRadius=90, streamingHysteresis=20, localEvent, soundEvent, soundOnOwner=true. Uses exact target incarnation, streaming reattachment and resource-owned cleanup. localEvent selects an owner entity graph (not a sound); soundEvent is separate. Target disappearance/body/bucket change invalidates the effect. The ID proves registry admission, not visible/audible playback. Attachment TTL defaults60000 ms and is bounded to1..600000 ms; slot/localSlot are at most64 bytes. Limits are2048 effects globally and512 per resource. weaponRight/localEvent are player-only.
example:
local id, err = Open77.effects.attach({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)},
 "electric.industrial_arm", {slot="RightHand",ttlMs=1500})
if not id then print(err); return end
-- Retain id and remove it when your action ends.

name: playOn
