summary: Play an ephemeral native effect on a typed target.
description: Requires world.effects. A bare target ID explicitly means player; typed targets avoid collisions between registries. name is a native entity effect event. options supports duration(default0),loop(defaultfalse),slot. Snapshot lifetime guards reject replaced targets; this one-shot is not replayed after streaming. Use attach for a durable owned effect.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.effects.playOn({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)}, nativeEvent, {duration=1})
if not ok then print(err) end

name: sound
summary: Play spatial sound on a typed target with optional action deduplication.
description: Requires world.effects. A bare target means player. options={unique=false,duration=5,actionId?,excludePlayers?}; duration is seconds and bounded by the backend. actionId is an opaque resource-scoped identity: repeated delivery of one contact does not replay sound. excludePlayers omits selected listeners, useful when native contact already supplies their audio. Sound targets carry current lifetime identity; no stale-body playback or durable late-stream replay is implied. duration is0.05..60 seconds; actionId is at most192 bytes and deduplication retains it for60 seconds without TTL renewal. excludePlayers accepts at most32 positive IDs; action identities are limited to8192 globally/4096 per resource.

name: cancel
summary: Cancel this resource's authoritative motion lease.
description: Requires players.motion.control. Requires the exact player and motion ID owned by the calling resource. Ends network ownership and requests native cleanup; collision/braking and get-up remain native, so cancellation need not instantly stop velocity or animation.
example:
local result, err = Open77.motion.cancel(playerId, motionId)
if not result then print(err) end

name: current
summary: Read an authoritative living-motion lease.
description: Requires players.motion.read. Returns {id,player,incarnation,bucket,directionX,directionY,distance,createdAt,expiresAt,phase,reason}, or nil. Times are server-monotonic milliseconds. pending awaits owner native ACK; active is not server-observed rendering. Acknowledged ownership lasts6s, including recovery; no generic teleport or map collision solution is provided.
example:
local motion = Open77.motion.current(playerId)
if motion then print(motion.id, motion.phase) end

name: knockdown
summary: Request bounded native living-player motion.
description: Requires players.motion.control. options={x,y,distance}; direction nonzero and normalized, distance0..6 m. Requires ready/alive/unmounted exact body and no existing lease; native owner additionally refuses unsuitable states. Returns admission, not damage or physical completion. onPlayerMotionChanged reports pending/active/ended; server pending expires after2s. Active snapshot checks are ACK-rooted, not exact native launch-origin enforcement.
example:
local result, err = Open77.motion.knockdown(playerId, {x=0,y=1,distance=0})
if not result then print(err) else print(result.id) end

name: getBehavior
summary: Reads the canonical behavior policy of an owned NPC.
description: Requires world.npcs. Returns a detached table with aiEnabled, combatEnabled, perceptionEnabled, voiceEnabled. Client inspection uses Open77.npcs.get(id).behavior with npcs.read.

name: setAIEnabled
summary: Pauses or resumes a server-owned NPC's native AI and Open77 tasks.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. Does not change aiMode or the other behavior options. Disabling revokes the simulation lease; enabling resumes according to the selected mode.

name: setBehavior
summary: Changes a server-owned NPC's native AI, combat, perception and voice policy.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. Partial boolean options aiEnabled, combatEnabled, perceptionEnabled, voiceEnabled; all default true. Replicated to observers and late joiners. See npc-behavior.md for engine semantics and boundaries.

name: setCombatEnabled
summary: Allows or suppresses a server-owned NPC's combat behavior.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. False clears threats, disables hostile acquisition/reactions and blocks outgoing hit processing without disabling scripted locomotion.

name: setPerceptionEnabled
summary: Controls autonomous sensory acquisition for a server-owned NPC.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. False disables senses, reactions and automatic threat seeding; does not cancel an existing explicit target. Combat or AI disabled takes precedence.

name: setVoiceEnabled
summary: Controls voice lines and barks of a server-owned NPC.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. Controls native voiceset lines/grunts (including combat/search barks), suppresses scripted voiceovers and filters native dialogue routed through subtitles. Replicated per NPC, not a global sound/SFX mute or a guarantee to stop audio already playing.

name: all
summary: Lists authoritative server vehicles.
description: Returns snapshots ordered by Open77 ID. An optional routing bucket filters the result; omitting it returns every vehicle visible to the resource.

name: breakAllGlass
summary: Breaks a range of vehicle glass elements.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Breaks the first `count` destructible-glass bits. The optional count defaults to all 32 and must be in 0..32.

name: breakGlass
summary: Breaks one vehicle glass element.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setGlassBroken(id, glass, true)`; the canonical bit is replicated and retained for late joiners.
example: Open77.vehicles.breakGlass(vehicleId, 0)

name: breakLight
summary: Breaks one vehicle light.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setLightBroken(id, index, true)`.

name: breakTire
summary: Breaks one vehicle tire.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setTireBroken(id, index, true)`. Tire indexes are 0..3.
example: Open77.vehicles.breakTire(vehicleId, 0)

name: closeDoor
summary: Closes a door, trunk, or hood.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setDoorOpen(id, door, false)`.

name: closeWindow
summary: Closes one side window.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setWindowOpen(id, window, false)`.

name: create
summary: Creates a server-authoritative network vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The definition selects the record, transform, routing bucket, appearance, optional authoritative paint, flags, health, and initial damage. The server allocates the Open77 ID and replicates the canonical vehicle to interested clients. The creator name is retained as provenance and cleanup scope, never as an exclusive mutation lock.

name: damageBodyCell
summary: Adds damage to one body cell.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Adds the amount to the current normalized cell and clamps the result to 0..1.

name: damageBodyZone
summary: Adds damage across a body zone.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Adds the amount to each selected body cell and clamps every result to 0..1.

name: detachPart
summary: Detaches one vehicle panel authoritatively.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setPartDetached(id, part, true)`. The state is replicated and retained for late join.
example: Open77.vehicles.detachPart(vehicleId, "bumperFront")

name: detachedParts
summary: Maps stable detached-part names to network bit indexes.
description: Read-only constants for trunk, hood variants, door variants and front/back bumpers. Indexes are append-only protocol values in the range 0..15.

name: forcePlayerOutOfVehicle
summary: Forces a player out of a network vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Publishes a durable forced-exit order and keeps the canonical seat reserved until the client confirms native unmount or the bounded transition timeout expires. This operation overrides an active exit lock. Supplying `vehicleId` protects against ejecting the player from a newer assignment by mistake.

name: get
summary: Returns one authoritative server vehicle snapshot.
description: Reads canonical identity, transform, flags, colors, all damage channels including detached parts, openings, occupants, and authority state. Returns `nil` for an unknown ID.

name: getDamage
summary: Returns the canonical damage snapshot.
description: Reads the server-owned body grid plus broken glass, light, tire, and detached-part masks. It returns `nil` when the vehicle ID is unknown.

name: getDamageProfile
summary: Returns a resource-local vehicle damage profile.
description: Reads the profile registered by the current server resource for the specified vehicle record. Profiles are not shared implicitly between resources.

name: getPaint
summary: Reads authoritative vehicle paint.
description: Returns `applied` plus keyed primary and secondary RGB tables. Pure black remains distinguishable from reset because `applied` is a separate canonical flag. Returns `nil` for an unknown vehicle ID.

name: getPlayerSeat
summary: Reads one player's canonical vehicle-seat assignment.
description: Returns the server ledger entry with vehicle ID, canonical seat name, numeric flags, and transition/policy booleans. It returns `nil` when the player is not assigned to a vehicle.

name: honk
summary: Alias of `Open77.vehicles.triggerHorn`.
description: Requires `world.vehicles` and uses the same current-owner routing, duration bounds, and transient synchronization contract as `triggerHorn`.

name: isDoorOpen
summary: Reads one canonical door opening state.
description: Server-side authoritative query covering four doors, trunk, and hood. Returns `nil` for an unknown vehicle ID.

name: isLocked
summary: Reads a vehicle's canonical entry-lock state.
description: Returns the derived durable lock boolean without requiring callers to decode the complete flags mask. Unknown vehicles return `nil`.

name: isPartDetached
summary: Reads one canonical detached-part bit.
description: Returns whether a named/indexed panel is detached, or `nil` when the vehicle ID is unknown.

name: isPlayerExitLocked
summary: Reports whether a player's canonical seat has exit lock enabled.
description: Returns true only when the player currently has a seat assignment carrying the durable `exitLocked` policy. An unseated or unknown player returns false.

name: isWindowOpen
summary: Reads one canonical side-window opening state.
description: Server-side authoritative query for indexes 0..3. It does not report broken glass and returns `nil` for an unknown vehicle.

name: lock
summary: Locks a vehicle against ordinary entry.
description: Convenience alias for `setLocked(id, true)`. Requires `world.vehicles` and updates durable canonical state.

name: openDoor
summary: Opens a door, trunk, or hood.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setDoorOpen(id, door, true)`.
example: Open77.vehicles.openDoor(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.doors.trunk)

name: openWindow
summary: Opens one side window.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setWindowOpen(id, window, true)`.

name: registerDamageProfile
summary: Registers resource-local named damage zones and glass parts.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Profiles are scoped to the calling server resource VM and can extend or override the default body-zone mapping for one vehicle record.

name: remove
summary: Removes a server-authoritative network vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Any authorized resource may remove any canonical vehicle, regardless of which resource created it. Removal clears occupancy and authority before notifying streamed clients.

name: removePlayerFromVehicle
summary: Alias for forced authoritative vehicle exit.
description: Same contract as `forcePlayerOutOfVehicle`, including the optional expected vehicle ID, exit-lock override, client confirmation, and timeout cleanup.

name: repair
summary: Repairs a selected vehicle damage scope.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Supported scopes are `glass`, `body`, `lights`, `tires`, `visual`, `mechanical`, and `full`. The default is `full`.
example: Open77.vehicles.repair(vehicleId, "visual")

name: repairAllGlass
summary: Repairs all vehicle glass.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the complete canonical broken-glass mask.

name: repairAllLights
summary: Repairs every vehicle light.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the complete canonical broken-light mask.

name: repairAllTires
summary: Repairs all four vehicle tires.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the complete canonical broken-tire mask.

name: repairBodyCell
summary: Repairs one body cell.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Sets the selected 1-based body cell to zero damage and replicates the repaired state.

name: repairBodyZone
summary: Repairs every body cell in a zone.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears all cells selected by a registered zone name or explicit index array.

name: repairGlass
summary: Repairs one vehicle glass element.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setGlassBroken(id, glass, false)`.

name: repairLight
summary: Repairs one vehicle light.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setLightBroken(id, index, false)`.

name: repairTire
summary: Repairs one vehicle tire.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setTireBroken(id, index, false)`.

name: resetPaint
summary: Restores a vehicle's authored paint.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the canonical custom-paint flag without treating stored RGB bytes as a sentinel, then reliably publishes the reset to all current and future viewers.

name: setBodyCell
summary: Sets one body-damage cell.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Lua body-cell indexes are 1..30 and the value is clamped or validated in the normalized 0..1 range.

name: setBodyDamage
summary: Replaces the complete body-damage grid.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The table must contain exactly 30 normalized finite values in the range 0..1.

name: setBodyZone
summary: Sets all body cells in a zone.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The zone may be a registered zone name or an explicit array of cell indexes. Every selected cell receives the normalized value.

name: setDamage
summary: Replaces multiple canonical damage components at once.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Accepts a combined damage table and validates body cells and bit masks before publishing one authoritative update.

name: setDetachedPartMask
summary: Adds a canonical detached-part mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The 16-bit mask is monotonic on a live projection. Removing a previously detached bit is rejected because REDengine 2.31 has no validated safe reattachment primitive.

name: setDoorMask
summary: Replaces the vehicle opening mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The six-bit mask covers four doors, trunk, and hood. Valid values are 0..63.

name: setDoorOpen
summary: Sets one door, trunk, or hood opening state.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `door` is an index 0..5 or one of the constants in `Open77.vehicles.doors`.

name: setGlassBroken
summary: Sets or clears one broken-glass bit.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `glass` may be a numeric 0..31 index or a name supplied by the resource's registered damage profile.

name: setGlassMask
summary: Replaces the broken-glass bit mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The 32-bit mask describes destructible glass records, not the four reversible side-window opening states.

name: setLightBroken
summary: Sets or clears one broken-light bit.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The light index must be in 0..31.

name: setLightMask
summary: Replaces the broken-light bit mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Replaces the complete 32-bit canonical broken-light mask.

name: setLocked
summary: Sets or clears a vehicle's durable entry lock.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Atomically changes only `VehicleStateFlags.Locked`, publishes the canonical result to current viewers and late joiners, and does not overwrite unrelated flags. This blocks ordinary entry, not exit by an existing occupant; forced server seat assignment may deliberately bypass it.

name: setPaint
summary: Sets authoritative paint on a canonical vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Accepts primary and optional secondary RGB colors as `#RRGGBB`, keyed `{ r, g, b }`, or positional tables. Omitting secondary mirrors primary. Paint is cross-resource and replicated to current viewers, stream-in projections, reconnects, and late joiners.

name: setPartDetached
summary: Detaches one standard vehicle part.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The part may be an index 0..15 or a name from `Open77.vehicles.detachedParts`. Only `true` is accepted; respawn the vehicle to restore panels.

name: setPlayerExitLocked
summary: Prevents or permits a player-controlled vehicle exit.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. While locked, native unmount and manual seat-switch attempts are rejected and reconciliation remounts any divergent local state. Seat policy is cross-resource, so an authorized gamemode or utility resource may coordinate vehicles created elsewhere. A server forced exit still overrides the lock. The optional vehicle ID is an optimistic guard against stale assignments.

name: setPlayerIntoVehicle
summary: Alias for authoritative player seat assignment.
description: Same contract as `warpPlayerIntoVehicle`. This name is useful to codebases that reserve `warp` for client presentation, while both server names create the same canonical seat assignment.

name: setTireBroken
summary: Sets or clears one broken tire.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Mutates one tire index in 0..3 and replicates the canonical state to streamed observers.

name: setTireMask
summary: Replaces the broken-tire bit mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Only the lower four bits are valid and correspond to tire indexes 0..3.

name: setTransform
summary: Moves a vehicle authoritatively.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Updates position and yaw, revokes any active physics lease, and publishes the new canonical transform to current viewers.

name: setWindowOpen
summary: Sets one reversible side-window opening state.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. This controls the four openable side windows and is separate from destructible broken-glass state.

name: triggerHorn
summary: Sounds a synchronized vehicle horn.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Sends a reliable, authority-epoch-bound one-shot command to the client currently simulating the vehicle. An unoccupied parked vehicle intentionally has no physics owner, so the server addresses all current viewers directly without granting a lease. Duration is 100..2000 ms and defaults to 250 ms. The event is transient and is not late-join state.

name: unlock
summary: Unlocks a vehicle for ordinary entry.
description: Convenience alias for `setLocked(id, false)`. Requires `world.vehicles` and updates durable canonical state.

name: update
summary: Updates canonical durable vehicle fields.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Applies only supplied fields, such as health, flags, colors, openings, tires, body damage, broken glass/lights, or detached parts. Any authorized resource may update any canonical vehicle; the authoritative result is replicated to current viewers and late joiners.

name: warpPlayerIntoVehicle
summary: Assigns a player to an authoritative vehicle seat.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The server reserves the seat immediately, optionally moves the player into the vehicle routing bucket, and keeps a durable forced-entry order until the target streams and the client confirms the native mount. Seat coordination is intentionally cross-resource: any resource with the permission may target any canonical vehicle. Proximity and the vehicle locked flag are bypassed; destroyed/exploded vehicles and occupied seats are rejected.

name: attachDriver
summary: Attaches a server-owned vehicle AI controller.
description: options.npcId optionally mounts an existing NPC owned by this resource; omission means driverless operation. Reserves the driver seat. Requires world.vehicles. Refuses occupied driver seats, destroyed vehicles, unsupported AV/Basilisk records and conflicting controllers. The NPC must be alive, in the same bucket and without active tasks. No NPC is created automatically.

name: chase
summary: Pursues a canonical entity using native autonomous pathing.
description: Same targetKind, targetId, speed, distance, behavior and timeout options as follow. Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. It does not enable weapon use, teleport catch-up, scripted ramming or police pursuit logic. Targets and simulator must remain in the same routing bucket.

name: driveTo
summary: Starts native autonomous driving to a world position.
description: Requires world.vehicles and this resource's attached controller. options.position={x,y,z} is required. Optional speed (0.5..55 m/s), arrivalRadius (1..20 m), timeoutMilliseconds (1000..3600000) and behavior. Returns a task state, or nil, reason. Acceptance is not arrival: subscribe to arrived, blocked or failed.

name: follow
summary: Continuously follows a canonical player, vehicle or NPC.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. options.targetKind is player, vehicle or npc and targetId is the canonical ID. Optional distance (3..80 m), speed, behavior and timeoutMilliseconds. Uses the native autonomous path follower with server-updated target coordinates, at most twice per second. Stops with target_unavailable if the target leaves the bucket or disappears.

name: followRoute
summary: Drives an ordered route of world points.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. options.points is an array of 1..64 {x,y,z} positions. Supports loop, speed, behavior, arrivalRadius and timeoutMilliseconds. Emits waypointReached at each point and arrived once at a non-looping route's end. This is a destination sequence, not an exact authored racing spline.

name: joinTraffic
summary: Starts indefinite native road-following.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. Uses the autonomous command's driveDownTheRoadIndefinitely mode; it does not spawn ambient traffic or use the solo Delamain taxi system. Supports speed, behavior and timeoutMilliseconds. No arrival event is expected; stop explicitly or handle failure/timeout.

name: on
summary: Subscribes to this resource's vehicle AI lifecycle events.
description: Requires a function callback. Events: waypointReached, arrived, cancelled, failed, blocked and resumed. The handler receives a decoded state table, not JSON text. Events are routed only to the controller's resource. blocked with reason=no_progress is a stall detector, not proof of an obstacle collision. No events are replayed; query state first.

name: removeDriver
summary: Stops AI control and releases its driver seat.
description: Requires world.vehicles and ownership of this AI controller. Cancels an active task and unmounts (but does not delete) the optional NPC, restoring its previous AI mode. Returns the detached state, or nil, reason.

name: setBehavior
summary: Selects normal, cautious or aggressive AI behavior.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. normal keeps native avoidance; cautious uses a 75% speed ceiling; aggressive enables native clearTrafficOnPath. These are bounded presets, not a promise of police AI or traffic-law compliance.

name: setSpeed
summary: Updates the native driving speed limit.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. speed is finite, 0.5..55 m/s; default 12. Changes the active command without restarting it each frame. Actual speed remains subject to road geometry, obstacles and the vehicle. Cautious behavior applies 75% of the configured ceiling.

name: state
summary: Reads authoritative vehicle AI state.
description: Requires world.vehicles. Returns the controller state or nil when no driver is attached. Contains vehicleId, npcId, taskId (strings), revision, mode, status, reason, speed, behavior, destination x/y/z, routeIndex/count, targetKind/id, distance, owner and epoch. Motion is still subject to the ordinary vehicle authority lease.

name: stop
summary: Cancels the active task and stops the vehicle.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. Idempotent. Keeps the AI controller and driver seat reserved for the next task. Emits cancelled once for an active task. Use removeDriver to release the seat.

name: accept
summary: Queue acceptance of the local player's offered invitation.
description: Declare dependency 'open77_player_interactions >=1.0.0'. This is an asynchronous resource-export facade: call from a managed coroutine and await the Promise; nil plus reason indicates dispatch/rejection. No presentation capability is required for consumers. Resolving a request ID means queued, not accepted by the server. Observe onPlayerInteractionResult or result(requestId), then lifecycle state events.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to request ID; nil, reason on rejection
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.playerInteractions.accept(interactionId)
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local value, rejected = pending:await()
    if rejected then print(rejected); return end
    print(value)
end)

name: attach
summary: Attach a resource-owned local prop to a rendered bone or vehicle.
description: Binding fields: parentType ('player' or 'vehicle'), parentId (canonical network ID, not an engine handle), bone (named slot, empty for root), offset {x,y,z} in metres (each ±20), rotation {x,y,z} in degrees (each ±360, local Z-Y-X composition). Unknown fields and non-finite numbers reject. Missing streamed parents are hidden, then rebound when available. See attachments.md. Requires world.props. This changes only this client's prop, not server authority. Physics uses a visual-only attachment host; arbitrary mesh paths without that host are refused.
example: local ok, err = Open77.props.attach(localPropId, {parentType='player', parentId=playerId, bone='RightHand'})

name: bones
summary: List available named attachment slots on a streamed parent.
description: Requires world.props. Returns sorted names from the current native slot components, not all skeleton bones. Parent IDs are canonical player/vehicle IDs. Empty array means unavailable or no slots; it does not establish that a different body/model supports a requested slot.
example:
local slots, err = Open77.props.bones('player', playerId)
if slots then for _, slot in ipairs(slots) do print(slot) end end

name: detach
summary: Detach a resource-owned local prop.
description: Requires world.props. Restores an independent host at the last locally rendered pose. Does not detach a server-owned network prop. Calling the server API is required for a replicated release.
example: local ok, err = Open77.props.detach(localPropId)

name: cancel
summary: Cancel an interaction owned by this resource.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Custom reason accepts 1–64 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore characters; invalid reasons normalize to cancelled. Delayed callbacks should retain the interaction ID, never cancel whatever action happens to occupy the player later.
example: local state, err = Open77.playerInteractions.cancel(interactionId, 'item_removed')

name: current
summary: Read the interaction reserving a player, including an unanswered invitation.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Terminal states are removed from the active registry. Read access never grants cancellation of another resource's action.
returns: active state or nil; nil, reason on rejection
example: local value, err = Open77.playerInteractions.current(playerId)

name: get
summary: Read a copied active state by opaque interaction ID.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. Clients cannot request broadcasts directly. getState reports intended playback, not decoder acknowledgement. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.

name: getHoloCallEyes
summary: Read the server-replicated blue eye-glow intent in the current routing bucket.
description: Requires players.holocall.read. Omit playerId for the local network player. Returns nil, state_unavailable before the initial server snapshot. False means absent from this client's active bucket snapshot; it is not a cross-bucket global query or proof that native pixels are rendered. There is intentionally no client setter. See holocall-eyes.md.
example: local enabled, reason = Open77.players.getHoloCallEyes()

name: getHoloCallEyes
summary: Read whether any server resource holds a player's holocall eye-glow lease.
description: Requires players.holocall.read and an explicit connected network player ID. This reads authoritative cosmetic intent, not a native render acknowledgement. False means no lease; nil, reason means the query failed. See holocall-eyes.md.
example: local enabled, reason = Open77.players.getHoloCallEyes(playerId)

name: setHoloCallEyes
summary: Synchronize a player's native blue holocall eye glow.
description: Requires players.holocall.control. Uses a network player ID, not an entity handle. Enabled must be a boolean; options may only contain durationMs (integer 0..600000, default 0). True acquires/renews this resource VM's lease; false releases only its lease. The glow remains enabled while any resource holds a lease. It clears on death, disconnect, resource stop/reload/failure or expiry. Reliable bucket snapshots cover late joins and re-stream; clients project onto native and F7 bodies. Does not open the phone UI or start a call. See holocall-eyes.md.
example: local ok, reason = Open77.players.setHoloCallEyes(playerId, true, { durationMs = 30000 })

name: configureThirdPerson
summary: Configures the playable third-person camera's framing, anchor, FOV and shoulder.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.style`. Acquires an exclusive resource-instance style or patches the caller's existing configuration. `style` selects `classic`, `shoulder` or `centered` and resets that preset before applying other fields; without it, fields patch the current configuration (classic on first use). `anchor` is `eyes` or `body` (feet), stable gameplay pivots rather than animated bones. `hip`, `aim` and `explore` accept distance (0.8..8 metres), offset (vector3 or complete x/y/z table: view-right -2..2, view-forward -1..1, world-up -1.5..3 metres), and fov (0 to restore the captured gameplay lens, otherwise 40..110 native component degrees). Other fields: shoulder (`left`/`right`), transition (0..3 seconds, default 0.3), runSpeed (0.5..15 m/s, default 2.5), runFov and sprintFov (0 disabled or 40..110). Aiming overrides sprint, which overrides running. Collision and native-camera safety still win. Unknown fields and invalid/non-finite values are rejected atomically. Does not enable TPP: use `Open77.perspective.setThirdPerson` separately. Stop/reload, coroutine failure and host teardown release the claim. Errors include `permission_denied:camera.style`, `camera_style_unavailable`, `invalid_camera_style_fields`, `invalid_camera_style` and `camera_style_owned`.

name: resetThirdPerson
summary: Releases this resource's camera style and shake, restoring underlying framing and FOV.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.style`. Releases the caller's style and shake and blends back to the underlying framing and captured gameplay lens. Does not turn third person off, clear a perspective lock or alter server policy. Safe when no style is configured; another resource's style returns `camera_style_owned` instead of being reset. Other errors: `permission_denied:camera.style`, `camera_style_unavailable`. Stop/reload, coroutine failure and host teardown also release the style automatically.
example:
-- Give the camera style back without changing the player's FPP/TPP choice.
local ok, reason = Open77.camera.resetThirdPerson()
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: shakeThirdPerson
summary: Starts or replaces a finite positional shake on the caller's playable TPP style.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.style` and a style already owned via configureThirdPerson. options: amplitude (vector3 or complete x/y/z table, each 0..0.2 metres, default 0.02/0.01/0.015), frequency (0.1..20 Hz, default 8), duration (0.05..10 seconds, default 0.5). Axes are view-right, view-forward, world-up. Shakes move the pivot before collision resolution; they do not rotate aim, inject roll or change player position. Natural attack/release envelope; a new shake replaces the old one rather than stacking. Wall-clock expiry continues while another camera owns the view. Unknown fields and invalid/non-finite values are refused. Errors: `permission_denied:camera.style`, `camera_style_unavailable`, `invalid_camera_shake`, `camera_style_not_owned`. Cleanup follows the owning style's lifecycle; do not restart it every frame.
example:
-- First acquire a style; an empty options table uses shake defaults.
local configured, reason = Open77.camera.configureThirdPerson({ style = "shoulder" })
if configured then
    Open77.camera.shakeThirdPerson({ amplitude = vector3(0.03, 0.015, 0.02), frequency = 8, duration = 0.65 })
else
    print(reason)
end

name: stopThirdPersonShake
summary: Immediately stops only the calling resource's third-person camera shake.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.style`. Safe when the caller owns no shake and never stops another resource's effect. Keeps the style and selected perspective unchanged. Explicit stop is immediate, unlike the natural expiry envelope. Errors: `permission_denied:camera.style`, `camera_style_unavailable`.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.camera.stopThirdPersonShake()
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: thirdPersonState
summary: Reads the requested third-person camera style and whether it is active or owned.
description: Client-only read; no permission required. Returns configured, owned (by the calling resource), active, shaking, appliedFov, and the full configuration: style, anchor, shoulder, hip/aim/explore (distance, offset, fov), transition, runSpeed, runFov and sprintFov. style names the base preset, even after custom patches. active is false while FPP, a native vehicle/scripted camera or wardrobe owns the view; a configured style resumes when the playable TPP rig returns. appliedFov is the last rig-written FOV, not necessarily the current camera's lens; use `Open77.camera.view()` for the rendered view. Returns `nil, camera_style_unavailable` when the backend is absent.
returns: snapshot table, or nil on failure
example:
local state, reason = Open77.camera.thirdPersonState()
if state then
    print(state.style, state.owned, state.active, state.appliedFov)
else
    print(reason)
end

name: setCinematic
summary: Hides gameplay HUD and nonfocused resource interfaces with animated letterbox bars.
description: Client-only; requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. enabled must be a boolean; optional height is a finite fraction of the viewport for EACH black bar, 0.01..0.4 (default 0.12). true holds a resource-instance cinematic claim; false releases only the caller's claim. Multiple resources cooperate and the greatest requested height wins. Masks native HUD including minimap, nonfocused Open77 WebUI pages including watermark/chat history/Freeroam HUD, and native world labels/debug overlays. Focused chat or menus remain accessible when opened, as does the developer console. Rendering is gated without destroying pages or changing their visibility state. Existing HUD hide claims, including the same resource's ordinary claims, survive release. Stop/reload, coroutine failure and host teardown clean up automatically. Does not change camera, pause gameplay, mute audio or affect other players. Distinct from the open77_uikit letterbox-only helper. Errors: `permission_denied:ui.vanilla.hud`, `invalid_cinematic_arguments`, `invalid_cinematic_height`, `cinematic_unavailable_on_this_host`.
example:
-- Manifest: permissions { "ui.vanilla.hud" }
local ok, reason = Open77.hud.setCinematic(true, 0.12)
if not ok then print(reason) end
-- At the end of the sequence, release only this resource's claim.
Open77.hud.setCinematic(false)

name: clearThirdPersonOverride
summary: Releases this resource's temporary FPP/TPP lock without changing player preference.
description: Client-only; no permission required and no arguments accepted. Idempotent: releases only the calling resource instance's override, never another resource's. Preserves the player's pre-lock preference, camera style and server perspective policy. Native-camera safety and server policy still determine the effective view after release. Stop/reload, coroutine failure and host teardown also release the owner's override automatically. To release a lock AND request a different view, use setThirdPerson(enabled, false) instead. Errors: `invalid_perspective_arguments`, `perspective_unavailable_on_this_host`.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.perspective.clearThirdPersonOverride()
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: setThirdPerson
summary: Requests first/third person, optionally locking that view for this resource.
description: Client-only. enabled and optional force must be strict booleans; force defaults to false. Ordinary true/false requests TPP/FPP without a permission and leaves F7 available, subject to existing locks and server policy. force=true requires `perspective.policy`: (true,true) locks TPP; (false,true) locks FPP. This exclusive resource-instance lock preserves the player's remembered pre-lock preference, including when F7 is pressed. A rival forced request returns `perspective_owned`. force=false first releases the caller's own previous lock, then requests the selected view; it cannot clear another resource's lock. Native vehicle/cutscene/safety states and server disabled/forced policy win. Conflicting server policy rejects a new lock with `refused_by_policy`; existing locks resume after policy permits them again. Stop/reload, coroutine failure and host teardown release the lock automatically. No per-frame loop is needed. Does not configure camera style or broadcast a network view: use server setPolicy for global policy. Other errors: `invalid_perspective_arguments`, `permission_denied:perspective.policy` (forced calls only), `perspective_unavailable_on_this_host`. Inspect state for the effective view rather than assuming acceptance means the TPP camera currently owns the screen.
example:
-- Manifest: permissions { "perspective.policy" }
local ok, reason = Open77.perspective.setThirdPerson(true, true)
if not ok then print(reason) end
-- Later restore the choice the player had before our lock.
Open77.perspective.clearThirdPersonOverride()

name: activate
summary: Acquires native input and begins editing an owned gizmo.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Rechecks the streamed target and incarnation, captures its current transform as the cancellation baseline and resets history. Refuses another input owner, a background game, dead player, vehicle/workspot or unsupported target. The tool must be visible. Re-activating an already active handle is idempotent. Emits activated; focus loss, target loss, timeout and owner stop cancel it.

name: active
summary: Reads this resource's active gizmo, if any.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Returns the active snapshot only when the calling resource generation owns it. Returns nil without an error when no tool is active or another resource owns the input lease. Only one gizmo can capture native cursor/keyboard input across all resources.

name: cancel
summary: Restores the activation baseline and ends editing.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Attempts to restore the original native transform, ends an active drag, releases only the editor's own holds and emits cancel/deactivated. Own-player/vehicle cursor input returns immediately but movement remains briefly fenced while restoration is observed; a newer normal travel/server placement wins. Those asynchronous adapters later emit settled with nativeTransform or error. A missing or replaced target cannot be recreated; cleanup still runs. The owned handle remains until destroy or resource teardown. Escape during a drag cancels that drag first; a second Escape cancels the session. See gizmos.md for asynchronous restoration failures.

name: capabilities
summary: Queries which transforms a target adapter supports.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Omit target for the virtual transform capabilities, or supply a typed target table with kind and id. Returns per-axis translate, rotate and scale booleans plus preview, commit and networked. The target must be attached. Native characters and props are yaw-only and native scaling is currently unsupported; virtual transforms support all axes. Never infer server authority from this query: commit=false on a network target means acceptance is a proposal, not a canonical mutation.

name: commit
summary: Accepts the current transform and ends editing.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Emits commit with the accepted transform and returns cursor input. Virtual targets retain data; supported local entities retain their pose. A network target requests restoration and emits a proposal only: the server must validate an edit ticket, ACL, identity, bucket, revision and bounds before applying its own authoritative mutation API. Local puppet placement and own-player/vehicle restoration report their asynchronous result through settled (with nativeTransform) or error. commit is not that completion acknowledgement, and settled never acknowledges server acceptance. This call neither sends a commit to the server nor grants authority. See gizmos.md.

name: create
summary: Creates a resource-owned native 3D gizmo.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Creates an inactive handle for a typed entity target or a virtual transform. It does not capture input until activate succeeds. Options include mode, space, axes, pivotOffset, snapping, bounds, size, timeoutMs and local preview. IDs and events are scoped to the exact resource VM and generation. Quotas are eight handles per owner and 64 globally. See gizmos.md for the full option schema, native capabilities, validation status and server-authority contract.

name: deactivate
summary: Cancels editing and releases the gizmo's input lease.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. This is an alias of cancel, not a hidden acceptance operation. Restores the activation baseline when the target still exists, releases owned native input/physics holds and emits cancel/deactivated. The handle remains available for querying or reactivation. Use commit to accept a result or destroy to remove the handle.

name: destroy
summary: Removes an owned gizmo, cancelling any active preview.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Cancels and releases an active tool before removing its handle and emitting destroyed. It never deletes the target entity. A previously committed local transform is not rolled back merely by destroying its inactive handle. Resource stop/reload performs equivalent owned-handle cleanup automatically.

name: get
summary: Reads one owned gizmo's complete snapshot.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Returns the same typed snapshot shape delivered to open77:gizmo events: current and initial transforms, target, capabilities, phase, active/dragging flags, handle, hover, options, revision and history counts. nativeTransform is false until asynchronous native completion, then contains the observed pose without overwriting the proposed transform. Target IDs are decimal strings. It refuses foreign or stale handles; no native pointer or VM identity is exposed. See gizmos.md.

name: list
summary: Lists this resource generation's gizmo snapshots.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Returns an array of owned snapshots, including idle and terminal handles until destroyed. It never lists another resource or VM's tools. Stop/reload destroys all owned handles and restores active previews. Use this query to reconcile state after coalesced events; do not assume an event for every rendered frame.

name: redo
summary: Reapplies an undone gizmo edit.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Restores the next transform in the active tool's history and previews it through the target adapter. Refuses an active drag, inactive handle or empty redo history. Any new accepted edit truncates the redo branch. Emits redo and updates the snapshot's history counts.

name: setTransform
summary: Applies a numeric transform edit to the active gizmo.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Applies a sparse transform table containing position, rotation and/or scale, retaining unspecified fields. Vectors require x/y/z; rotation requires normalized x/y/z/w. Rejects non-finite values, unsupported target axes, bounds violations, inactive handles and active drags. A changed value is previewed locally, added to history and emitted as change. It is not an authoritative server mutation.

name: undo
summary: Undoes the last completed gizmo edit.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Restores the preceding transform in the active tool's bounded history and previews it through the target adapter. A completed drag is one history entry; numeric setTransform edits also create entries. Refuses an active drag, inactive handle or empty undo history. Emits undo. History stores at most 32 undo steps and resets on activation.

name: update
summary: Reconfigures an owned gizmo without replacing its target.
description: Client-only; requires gizmos.edit. Applies a validated sparse patch of mode, space, axes, pivotOffset, snap, position/scale bounds, visible and size. Target, transform, preview and timeout are creation-time settings and cannot be changed here. Refuses changes during a drag, unsupported modes and hiding the active gizmo. Emits configured. Axis restrictions control pointer handles; target capabilities and bounds also constrain numeric edits.
